records.name: ListEdgeColouring.gale_shapley
records.entry_name: Galvin's theorem for bipartite multigraphs, the Dinitz problem and stable matchings
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Galvin’s theorem for finite bipartite multigraphs: every assignment of finite edge lists of size at least the maximum incidence degree admits a proper edge coloring, with parallel edges counted separately. It includes ordinary edge coloring with Δ colors and the matching lower bound, and the Borodin–Kostochka–Woodall theorem for local lists (lists of size at least the larger degree of the two ends of each edge suffice). The previously registered simple-graph Galvin theorem, Dinitz problem and Gale–Shapley stable matching theorem are retained.

records.name: CountingSTS.N_le_D
records.entry_name: Counting Steiner triple systems: Wilson (1974) and Linial–Luria (2013)
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of R. M. Wilson's "Nonisomorphic Steiner triple systems" (inequality (2.1), Theorems 1–4, Lemmas 3–5, including the exact numbers of Latin squares of orders 6, 7 and 8 and the bounds N(19) ≥ 2450, N(21) ≥ 2160980, N(25) ≥ 163929929318400) and of N. Linial and Z. Luria's "An upper bound on the number of Steiner triple systems" (Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 with explicit error terms). Version 2 adds a proof of the van der Waerden permanent theorem (Egorychev, Falikman), following Gurvits's proof as simplified by Laurent and Schrijver. The parts of Wilson's Theorems 2 and 3 that rely on it are stated both as implications from the hypothesis vdWPC, as in the paper, and unconditionally (theorem2_full, theorem3_full). Finite computations are kernel-checked certificates (no native_decide). Mathlib does not contain these results.

records.name: LeanLab.HardyLittlewood1923.theoremB
records.entry_name: Sums of primes, after Hardy and Littlewood 1923, Partitio Numerorum III, Theorems B to F proved without Hypothesis R, and Theorem A on Hypothesis R for 47/64 at most Theta below 3/4
records.doc: A sorry-free Lean 4 proof, with no hypothesis, of Theorems B, C, D, E and F of G. H. Hardy and J. E. Littlewood, Some problems of Partitio Numerorum III, Acta Math. 44, 1923. Hardy and Littlewood proved these theorems on their Hypothesis R, a form of the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions; here they are proved unconditionally, from Vinogradov's estimate for exponential sums over primes and the Siegel-Walfisz theorem, so the argument is not Hardy and Littlewood's own for Theorems B, D and E. Formalized: Theorem B, the asymptotic for the weighted count nu_r of n as an ordered sum of r primes, for every r at least 3 and n of the parity of r, with the singular series written as the paper's product over the odd primes dividing n, and nu_r of n is o of n^{r-1} for unlike parity; Theorem C, N_r of n is asymptotic to nu_r of n over log^r n; Theorem D, the ternary asymptotic with the constant C_3 and every large odd number a sum of three odd primes; Theorem E, the asymptotic for four odd primes, every large even number a sum of four odd primes, one of which may be assigned; and Theorem F, that an asymptotic of Conjecture A's shape for binary Goldbach can only carry the constant 2 C_2, together with a check that the printed formula 4.23 has a misprint. Version 2 adds Theorem A, eq 3.113: for every r at least 3 and every Theta with 47/64 at most Theta below 3/4, on the paper's own Hypothesis R at level Theta, that no Dirichlet L-function has a zero with real part above Theta, nu_r of n equals the singular series S_r of n of 3.114 times n^{r-1} over the factorial of r minus 1, plus O of n^{r-1+Theta-3/4} times a power of log n, for all n from some n0. The paper allows every Theta below 3/4; the Lean statement covers only 47/64 at most Theta below 3/4. The entry also proves derived results on Theorem A that are not statements of the paper: its hypotheses other than the zero-free one hold together, GRH gives the zero-free hypothesis for every Theta at least 1/2, Theorem A at Theta equal to 47/64 on GRH, and S_r of n is positive with a summable series in like parity. Ternary Goldbach is Helfgott's theorem; binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. The Lean code was written by an AI agent; the statements were written from the paper's page images by AI agents and are offered for human audit.

records.entry_name: Sums of primes, after Hardy and Littlewood 1923, Partitio Numerorum III, Theorems B to F proved without Hypothesis R, and Theorem A on Hypothesis R for 47/64 at most Theta below 3/4
records.doc: A sorry-free Lean 4 proof, with no hypothesis, of Theorems B, C, D, E and F of G. H. Hardy and J. E. Littlewood, Some problems of Partitio Numerorum III, Acta Math. 44, 1923. Hardy and Littlewood proved these theorems on their Hypothesis R, a form of the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions; here they are proved unconditionally, from Vinogradov's estimate for exponential sums over primes and the Siegel-Walfisz theorem, so the argument is not Hardy and Littlewood's own for Theorems B, D and E. Formalized: Theorem B, the asymptotic for the weighted count nu_r of n as an ordered sum of r primes, for every r at least 3 and n of the parity of r, with the singular series written as the paper's product over the odd primes dividing n, and nu_r of n is o of n^{r-1} for unlike parity; Theorem C, N_r of n is asymptotic to nu_r of n over log^r n; Theorem D, the ternary asymptotic with the constant C_3 and every large odd number a sum of three odd primes; Theorem E, the asymptotic for four odd primes, every large even number a sum of four odd primes, one of which may be assigned; and Theorem F, that an asymptotic of Conjecture A's shape for binary Goldbach can only carry the constant 2 C_2, together with a check that the printed formula 4.23 has a misprint. Version 2 adds Theorem A, eq 3.113: for every r at least 3 and every Theta with 47/64 at most Theta below 3/4, on the paper's own Hypothesis R at level Theta, that no Dirichlet L-function has a zero with real part above Theta, nu_r of n equals the singular series S_r of n of 3.114 times n^{r-1} over the factorial of r minus 1, plus O of n^{r-1+Theta-3/4} times a power of log n, for all n from some n0. The paper allows every Theta below 3/4; the Lean statement covers only 47/64 at most Theta below 3/4. The entry also proves derived results on Theorem A that are not statements of the paper: its hypotheses other than the zero-free one hold together, GRH gives the zero-free hypothesis for every Theta at least 1/2, Theorem A at Theta equal to 47/64 on GRH, and S_r of n is positive with a summable series in like parity. Ternary Goldbach is Helfgott's theorem; binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. records.name: NormalizerLean.helling
records.entry_name: Helling's theorem: the maximal subgroups of SL₂(ℝ) commensurable with SL₂(ℤ)
records.doc: Formal statements and proofs, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, of Helling's theorem and of consequences for normalizers. A subgroup G ≤ SL₂(ℝ) is commensurable with SL₂(ℤ) if G ∩ SL₂(ℤ) has finite index in G and in SL₂(ℤ); Γ₀(N)⁺ is the group generated by the Atkin–Lehner elements of level N, and contains Γ₀(N). Every G commensurable with SL₂(ℤ) is conjugate into Γ₀(N)⁺ for some squarefree N, by (det A)^{−1/2}·A for an integral matrix A with det A > 0. For every N ≥ 1, Γ₀(N)⁺ is commensurable with SL₂(ℤ), and for squarefree N it is maximal among such groups; so the maximal subgroups of SL₂(ℝ) commensurable with SL₂(ℤ) are the conjugates of the Γ₀(N)⁺, N squarefree, that are commensurable with SL₂(ℤ) (Duncan's Theorem 2.11, in SL₂(ℝ)), and Γ₀(4)⁺ is not maximal. The commensurator of SL₂(ℤ) in SL₂(ℝ) consists of the (det A)^{−1/2}·A. For every Γ commensurable with SL₂(ℤ), the normalizer of Γ in SL₂(ℝ) is commensurable with SL₂(ℤ), so Nor(Γ)/Γ is finite, and Nor(Γ) is conjugate into Γ₀(N)⁺ for some squarefree N. The proof is the argument with p-adic trees that Duncan attributes to Conway, with an integral matrix for each vertex and distances computed from p-adic valuations of determinants and of the gcd of the entries; the vertices and edges fixed at the different primes are glued with the Smith normal form. 9 theorems, no sorry, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: OpenPolish.imageStrategy_winning
records.entry_name: Continuous open images of Polish spaces
records.doc: Continuous open surjections preserve the strong Choquet property in arbitrary topological spaces. An explicit full-history strategy lifts each legal target play coherently, keeps the marked point, and maps an actual common source point. Consequently a continuous open metrizable image of a Polish space is Polish. A second-countable completely metrizable source gives a completely metrizable metrizable image. A regular Hausdorff codomain also suffices, by inherited second countability and Urysohn metrizability. These are classical results; no novelty or priority is claimed.

records.name: ExpanderTheorem.expander_mixing
records.entry_name: The expander mixing lemma and the Alon–Boppana bound
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of two basic results of spectral graph theory, stated through the adjacency quadratic form on vectors orthogonal to the all-ones vector: the expander mixing lemma of Alon and Chung (for a d-regular graph on n ≥ 2 vertices with |x·Ax| ≤ μ‖x‖² on 𝟙⊥, |e(S,T) − d|S||T|/n| ≤ μ√(|S||T|)), and the Alon–Boppana bound in Nilli's form (a d-regular graph, d ≥ 2, with two vertices at distance at least 2k + 4 has a nonzero x ⟂ 𝟙 with x·Ax ≥ (2√(d−1) − (2√(d−1) − 1)/(k+1))‖x‖²). Mathlib has adjacency matrices but neither result.

records.name: ExpanderTheorem.alon_boppana
records.entry_name: The expander mixing lemma and the Alon–Boppana bound
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of two basic results of spectral graph theory, stated through the adjacency quadratic form on vectors orthogonal to the all-ones vector: the expander mixing lemma of Alon and Chung (for a d-regular graph on n ≥ 2 vertices with |x·Ax| ≤ μ‖x‖² on 𝟙⊥, |e(S,T) − d|S||T|/n| ≤ μ√(|S||T|)), and the Alon–Boppana bound in Nilli's form (a d-regular graph, d ≥ 2, with two vertices at distance at least 2k + 4 has a nonzero x ⟂ 𝟙 with x·Ax ≥ (2√(d−1) − (2√(d−1) − 1)/(k+1))‖x‖²). Mathlib has adjacency matrices but neither result.

records.name: PalomarCorpus.E251.PaperStatementsA.bounded_test_finite_coupling
records.entry_name: Uniform sparse rationalisation of dyadic series
records.doc: Given any convergent dyadic series with nonnegative integer coefficients, any finite prefix and any eventually unbounded correction allowance, one common permitted set of upper Banach density zero supports nonnegative integer corrections realising every target in a nondegenerate interval above the original sum. Each fixed modulus eventually divides both corrections and cumulative corrections beyond a cutoff independent of the target. With polylogarithmic allowance, the selected theorem also bounds support in dyadic windows and preserves empirical block distributions in total variation for lengths o(log log X), uniformly in the target. The entry additionally states exact prime-to-gap summation identities and tail rationality criteria. It does not select the prime-gap joint countermodel, which in the paper uses named outside inputs, and makes no claim that corrected cumulative positions are prime or that the original prime series is irrational.

records.name: PalomarCorpus.E269.PaperStatementsA.dyadicBlockBase235_cases
records.entry_name: Infinite rank of the three-prime running-LCM kernel
records.doc: For pairwise distinct primes p, q and r, the three-prime reciprocal running-LCM kernel has nonzero square minors of every order, with row and column indices chosen independently of the third exponent. Consequently it admits no finite rational separated representation. The selected entry also proves an exact rank formula for threshold-column matrices, an explicit two-by-two example at 2,3,5, separation in the two-prime comparison, and the four-base dyadic recurrence for the actual 2,3,5 sum. A uniform finite-rank approximation statement concerns the rescaled carry matrix. The stronger unit-determinant modular minors are in E269_08 and are outside this configuration. Infinite kernel rank does not prove irrationality of the running-LCM series. In the selected rank theorem the determinants remain nonzero for every fixed third exponent k using the same injective row and column maps. The distance theorem concerns a rescaled real carry matrix and is not an approximation lower bound for the original summable kernel.

records.name: OpenBaire.exists_open_refinement
records.entry_name: Open Baire-space representation of Polish spaces
records.doc: Every nonempty Polish space is the image of Baire space, the product of countably many discrete natural-number spaces, under a continuous open surjection. The proof constructs a countably branching nonempty open scheme with nested closures, covering children and geometrically shrinking diameters. The image of each basic cylinder is proved exactly equal to its scheme open set. This yields openness and surjectivity of the limit map; existence is also characterized by nonemptiness. These are classical results, with no novelty or priority claim.

records.name: BaireCharacterization.exists_clopen_partition
records.entry_name: Alexandrov–Urysohn characterization of Baire space
records.doc: A topological space is homeomorphic to Baire space, the countable product of discrete natural numbers, if and only if it is nonempty, Polish, has a basis of clopen sets, and every compact subset has empty interior. The construction partitions each nonempty clopen set into countably infinitely many distinct nonempty clopen children with arbitrarily small diameter. A fully branching shrinking scheme gives a continuous open bijective limit map and therefore a homeomorphism. The converse uses finite coordinate images of compact Baire subsets. This formalizes a classical theorem of Alexandrov and Urysohn; no novelty or priority claim is made.

records.doc: A topological space is homeomorphic to Baire space, the countable product of discrete natural numbers, if and only if it is nonempty, Polish, has a basis of clopen sets, and every compact subset has empty interior. The construction partitions each nonempty clopen set into countably infinitely many distinct nonempty clopen children with arbitrarily small diameter. A fully branching shrinking scheme gives a continuous open bijective limit map and therefore a homeomorphism. The converse uses finite coordinate images of compact Baire subsets. This formalizes a classical theorem of Alexandrov and Urysohn; no novelty or priority claim is made.

records.name: BondySimonovitsTheorem.bondy_simonovits
records.entry_name: The Bondy–Simonovits even cycle theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Bondy–Simonovits theorem: for every k ≥ 2 there is a constant C such that every finite simple graph on n vertices with no cycle of length exactly 2k has at most C·n^(1+1/k) edges, i.e. ex(n, C_2k) = O(n^(1+1/k)). The statement is existential in C (the proof gives C = 16k + 4); the sharper constants of later work and the full range of even cycle lengths in Bondy–Simonovits's paper are not stated. Mathlib has walks and cycles but not this theorem.

records.name: CantorCharacterization.exists_clopen_split
records.entry_name: Brouwer characterization of Cantor space
records.doc: A topological space is homeomorphic to Cantor space, the countable product of discrete Boolean spaces, if and only if it is nonempty, compact, metrizable, has a basis of clopen sets, and has no isolated points. A full binary clopen scheme decides an enumerated basis one element at each depth. Its point-address map is continuous; compact nested intersections realize every binary branch, and basis decisions separate points. A continuous bijection from a compact space to the Hausdorff Cantor space is a homeomorphism. This formalizes a classical theorem of Brouwer; no mathematical novelty or priority claim is made.

records.name: PalomarNivat.nivat
records.entry_name: Nivat's conjecture
records.doc: For every configuration on the integer plane over an arbitrary finite alphabet, a positive k by n rectangle with at most k*n occurring translated patterns forces a nonzero global period of the original configuration. The statement includes equality at the complexity threshold and rectangles of width or height one. The Lean proof is due to Catenation, my custom agentic framework, translating the argument in my paper into Lean. The proof uses Laurent annihilators, a sharp periodic-wedge complexity bound, generating polygons, and selection of the same nonperiodic orbit point throughout the periodic-background construction. Its mathematical setting is multidimensional symbolic dynamics and combinatorics of low-complexity configurations. The independent Challenge states the full conjecture using only standard Mathlib notions.

records.name: SierpinskiRationals.countable_hasClopenBasis
records.entry_name: Sierpiński's characterization of the rationals
records.doc: Every nonempty countable metrizable topological space without isolated points is homeomorphic to the rational numbers with their usual topology. Conversely, these four properties characterize spaces homeomorphic to the rationals. A clopen basis is derived from the hypotheses. Scheduled binary clopen splits give each point an address with both bits arbitrarily far out; the induced lexicographic order is proved dense, without endpoints, and to generate exactly the original topology. The countable dense-order isomorphism theorem then gives the homeomorphism. This formalizes classical mathematics; no mathematical novelty or priority claim is made.

records.name: MultiplicativeBasisDeformations.Challenge.theoremA
records.entry_name: Multiplicative bases and standardness of representation-finite algebras
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 formalization, built on Mathlib, of two classical theorems of Bautista, Gabriel, Roiter and Salmerón on finite-dimensional representation-finite algebras over an algebraically closed field. Theorem A: every such algebra, in any characteristic, has a normed multiplicative basis, that is, a basis containing a complete set of primitive orthogonal idempotents, closed under products up to zero, and meeting every power of the Jacobson radical in a basis of that power. Theorem B: every basic such algebra over a field of characteristic different from two is standard, that is, its category of indecomposable modules is equivalent to the mesh category of its Auslander–Reiten quiver by an equivalence sending each vertex to its module. The proof follows the deformation-theoretic approach of the formalized manuscript: the standard form is the graded algebra of the radical filtration of the category of indecomposable modules, and the original algebra is recovered as a filtered deformation of it. The Auslander–Reiten theory used is proved in the library.

records.name: Planarwave.vHJ_approximates_planar_front
records.entry_name: Stability of planar fronts in reaction-diffusion systems
records.doc: A Lean formalization of effective dynamics near spectrally stable planar fronts in reaction-diffusion systems under small, bounded uniformly continuous perturbations. The main result constructs global solutions and approximates the perturbed front by a phase evolving according to a viscous Hamilton-Jacobi equation, with a uniform quantitative error bound.

records.name: GrahamPollakTheorem.graham_pollak
records.entry_name: The Graham–Pollak theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Graham–Pollak theorem: the edge set of the complete graph K_n cannot be partitioned into fewer than n − 1 complete bipartite graphs, together with the matching construction by n − 1 stars. Biclique decompositions are encoded by families of pairs of disjoint vertex sets covering every pair of distinct vertices exactly once. Mathlib does not contain this theorem.

records.name: GroupDimension.Palomar.D_five_eq_gamma_five_of_exp_three
records.entry_name: Fifth dimension subgroups: D₅ = γ₅ when G/γ₂ is finite of exponent 3, candidates for a counterexample, and a reduction of Kourovka 20.84
records.doc: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization accompanying S. Vorobev, "On the inclusion D_5(G) ⊆ γ_4(G): reductions, the Lie-ring proof, and evidence" (preprint, 2026; submitted to arXiv math.GR on 2026-10-22). The integral dimension subgroups D_n(G) = {g ∈ G : g − 1 ∈ Δ(G)^n} are defined from the augmentation ideal of Mathlib's integral group ring. Kourovka Problem 20.84 asks whether D_5(G) ⊆ γ_4(G) for every group; it is open and is not claimed here. Unconditional results: D_5(G) = γ_5(G) whenever G/γ_2(G) is finite of exponent 3, and more generally whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite 3-group whose cubes form a cyclic group (paper, Theorems 6.6 and 6.8; the inclusion part of Tahara's 1981 description of D_5 is formalized for this); D_5(G) lies in the Jennings product M_5(G) for finite 2-groups of class at most 3; and, for "candidates" (the paper's minimal-counterexample shape among finite 2-groups of class 3), there is no candidate of order 2^11 with Q/P_3 ≅ Z/4 × (Z/2)^7 and none of order 2^11 and rank at least 8 (paper, Lemma 5.6 and Proposition 5.7). Conditional results, with every assumption an explicit hypothesis: the reduction of Problem 20.84 to finite 2-groups of class exactly 3 assuming D_3 = γ_3, Passi's D_4^2 ⊆ γ_4 and Gruenberg's residual theorem (Proposition 2.1); a minimal counterexample is a candidate assuming D_3 = γ_3 (Lemma 5.2); and D_5 = 1 for groups of order 2^11, class at most 3 and rank at least 8, assuming D_3 = γ_3 and the paper's computer result for order 2^10 (Proposition 5.7, D_5 form).

records.name: PalomarSIL.mathematical_result
records.entry_name: Control flow obfuscation with irreducible loops and self-modifying code
records.doc: Lean 4 development (no Mathlib) of the mathematics, algorithms and security statements of Morse, Alqaradaghi and Kozsik, "Control flow obfuscation with irreducible loops and self-modifying code": a self-modifying-code solver for 2-SAT and the planted instance generator as an algorithm, the extremal numbers of irreducible loops and multiple-entry edges (the families Kn and Mn), the irreducible-loop transformations of Figures 5 and 6, the Boolean control-flow graphs of AES, and the security statements of Section 5.1 relative to an explicit structural threat model. Two Challenges are submitted from one development: Challenge.lean (solver, extremal numbers, transformations, security model) and ChallengeAES.lean (the AES graphs); a Challenge may have at most 1,000 lines.

records.name: TemporalCliqueSpanners.exists_isTemporalSpanner_card_le
records.entry_name: Temporal cliques admit spanners of size O(n log n)
records.doc: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the theorem that every temporal clique on n vertices admits a temporal spanner with O(n log n) edges. A temporal clique is the complete graph on a finite vertex set whose edges carry natural-number time labels, locally injective (two edges sharing an endpoint have distinct labels); a temporal spanner is a set of edges in which every vertex reaches every other one by a journey with non-decreasing labels. The result is due to Casteigts, Peters and Schoeters (ICALP 2019, JCSS 2021); the formal proof follows the dismountability-only proof of Carnevale, Casteigts and Corsini (SAND 2025, §§2–4), which reduces cliques to bi-cliques and concludes with the one-sided dismountability of Angrick et al. (ESA 2024). The compared statements give an explicit bound of 2n⌈log₂ n⌉ + 4n edges and the asymptotic O(n log n) form with a bound function chosen uniformly for all cliques. The work is supervised by Arnaud Casteigts and Karine Altisen.

records.name: ProjectiveDecay.rp2_log_square
records.entry_name: Log-square quadrupolar correlation decay in two-dimensional RP2 and RP3 models
records.doc: For the two-dimensional nearest-neighbor RP2 and RP3 director models, the absolute quadrupolar two-point correlation is bounded by C exp(-c (log(2+r))^2) at every finite bound on the dimensionless coupling. The positive constants are uniform over finite square-lattice subgraphs, arbitrary signed edge couplings within that bound, and observation sites; r is the integer lattice infinity distance. The compared statements use explicit normalized spherical product measures and Gibbs-integral quotients, with observable (n_x dot n_y)^2 - 1/3 or - 1/4, respectively. No response estimate or decay certificate is assumed. This registry interface selects the two finite-volume bounds. It does not assert exponential decay at all temperatures or the absence of every thermodynamic or topological transition. The larger development also contains local-limit and high-temperature results, which are not selected by this Comparator entry.

records.name: DGSMain.almost_all_graphs_are_DGS
records.entry_name: Almost all graphs are determined by their generalized spectrum
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the theorem that almost all graphs are determined by their generalized spectrum, which is Haemers' conjecture for the generalized spectrum. The generalized spectrum of a graph is the spectrum of its adjacency matrix A together with the spectrum of the adjacency matrix J - I - A of its complement, and a graph is determined by its generalized spectrum (DGS) if every graph with the same generalized spectrum is isomorphic to it. The main theorem, DGSMain.almost_all_graphs_are_DGS, states that the proportion of the graphs on the vertex set {0, ..., n-1} that are DGS tends to 1 as n tends to infinity; that is, the random graph G(n, 1/2) is DGS with probability tending to one. This is Theorem 1.1 of the accompanying paper, and the formalization contains its whole proof: the reduction to local failures at primes through the rational orthogonal matrices relating generalized cospectral graphs, Seidel switching, Fourier analysis of random symmetric matrices over finite rings, inverse Littlewood-Offord estimates over finite fields, rank estimates for random symmetric matrices modulo primes, and the exclusion of rational factors of the characteristic polynomial of a random symmetric sign matrix with zero diagonal. The results that the paper quotes from the literature are also proved: Kneser's addition theorem, the theorem of Johnson and Newman on generalized cospectral graphs, and the cases used of the theorems of Tao and Vu (a random symmetric sign matrix has simple spectrum) and of O'Rourke and Touri (G(n, 1/2) is controllable), the last two by a new argument based on the methods of the paper. The proof uses only the standard axioms propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice.

records.name: ShortGCD.generates_G
records.entry_name: The Euclidean algorithm is not optimal among uniform processes
records.doc: For every pair a ≥ b ≥ 1 there is a straight-line derivation of gcd(a, b) that uses only the remainder operation on available values and makes at most (3 + o(1)) log₂ a / log₂ log₂ a remainder calls, uniformly in b ≤ a; Euclid's algorithm needs about 1.44 log₂ a calls in the worst case. The proof stores a prefix of the Euclidean remainder sequence, shows that modulo every sufficiently large modulus at most three of its values share a residue class, and uses close residues to shrink the modulus by three remainder calls at a time. Consequently the intrinsic calls(rem)-complexities of the gcd and of coprimeness, in the sense of Moschovakis's Abstract Recursion and Intrinsic Complexity, are O(log a / log log a). This refutes Conjecture 3.4 of Moschovakis's 2012 notes "Absolute lower bounds for uniform processes" and the version (4F-5) of the Main Conjecture in the book, both for the structure (ℕ, rem, eq0) and for Nε = (ℕ, rem, eq0, eq1). The same bound answers negatively the closure-depth question of van den Dries and Moschovakis (2009): there are no positive integers aₙ → ∞, bₙ and C > 0 whose closure depth g(aₙ, bₙ) exceeds C log₂ aₙ for all n. For algorithms, the library gives fixed nondeterministic register programs over (ℕ, rem, eq0) with arbitrarily small logarithmic coefficients: for each ε > 0, one program with 3·2^p + 6 registers (any p > 3/ε) and no recursion stack has, on every input a ≥ b ≥ 1, a convergent computation returning gcd(a, b) with at most ε log₂ a + B remainder calls, and the same program written one function per line is a tail-recursive program with bounded stacks. These programs depend on ε, so the Main Conjecture for algorithms (deterministic or nondeterministic recursive programs) is not settled and remains open. Lower bounds are also formalized: every gcd certificate needs at least as many remainder facts as the shortest derivation, and the coprimeness complexity is at least (1 − ε) log₂ log₂ N on all but o(N²) coprime pairs below N.

The proof stores a prefix of the Euclidean remainder sequence, shows that modulo every sufficiently large modulus at most three of its values share a residue class, and uses close residues to shrink the modulus by three remainder calls at a time. Consequently the intrinsic calls(rem)-complexities of the gcd and of coprimeness, in the sense of Moschovakis's Abstract Recursion and Intrinsic Complexity, are O(log a / log log a). This refutes Conjecture 3.4 of Moschovakis's 2012 notes "Absolute lower bounds for uniform processes" and the version (4F-5) of the Main Conjecture in the book, both for the structure (ℕ, rem, eq0) and for Nε = (ℕ, rem, eq0, eq1). The same bound answers negatively the closure-depth question of van den Dries and Moschovakis (2009): there are no positive integers aₙ → ∞, bₙ and C > 0 whose closure depth g(aₙ, bₙ) exceeds C log₂ aₙ for all n. For algorithms, the library gives fixed nondeterministic register programs over (ℕ, rem, eq0) with arbitrarily small logarithmic coefficients: for each ε > 0, one program with 3·2^p + 6 registers (any p > 3/ε) and no recursion stack has, on every input a ≥ b ≥ 1, a convergent computation returning gcd(a, b) with at most ε log₂ a + B remainder calls, and the same program written one function per line is a tail-recursive program with bounded stacks. These programs depend on ε, so the Main Conjecture for algorithms (deterministic or nondeterministic recursive programs) is not settled and remains open. Lower bounds are also formalized: every gcd certificate needs at least as many remainder facts as the shortest derivation, and the coprimeness complexity is at least (1 − ε) log₂ log₂ N on all but o(N²) coprime pairs below N.

records.doc: Typed triangle decomposition results from Paper II: a typical-host theorem under three-step links for four-label families; its nearly complete and balanced deductions with explicit type-weight hypotheses; a semidense two-label mixed-triangle theorem; a computer-assisted typical-host theorem for every admissible four-label family; and a terminal absorber obtained from a bounded signed certificate and explicit physical hinge supply. Divisibility includes global edge counts and local degree profiles. The typical-host hypotheses are retained; the result is not asserted for arbitrary divisible hosts. The repository contains the substantive proof development, including the finite family census and conserved-family constructions, with a small independent Mathlib-only Challenge.

records.name: Erdos1063.erdos_1063.variants.lower_bound
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem 1063: a lower bound for n_k and the structure of the exceptional index
records.doc: For k ≥ 2 let n_k be the least n ≥ 2k such that n − i divides the binomial coefficient C(n, k) for all but exactly one 0 ≤ i < k (Erdős Problem 1063; Erdős and Selfridge 1983; OEIS A389360; Guy's Unsolved Problems in Number Theory, B31). Using the definition of n_k from google-deepmind/formal-conjectures verbatim, this project proves two results in Lean 4 with Mathlib. (1) For every k ≥ 2, n_k ≥ W'_k = ∏_{p^a ∥ k} p^(a + ⌊log_p(k − 1)⌋); the bound is attained in the sense that n_k − i₀ = W'_k for k = 4, 6, 14. (2) If n ≥ 2k, e < k, and every n − i with 0 ≤ i < k, i ≠ e, divides C(n, k), then e = n mod k and D(k, e) = ∏_{p^a ∥ k} p^(a + v_p(C(k − 1, e)) + ⌊log_p max(e, k − 1 − e)⌋) divides n − e. Result (2) was proved informally by the user rickyc in the erdosproblems.com discussion thread for the problem. It is the structural input of the exhaustive searches that extend the OEIS table (by jbell31 for 60 ≤ k ≤ 75, and by the author for k up to 140): an admissible n with exceptional index e must lie in the residue class e modulo D(k, e). This formalization makes the minimality of those computed values depend only on verified mathematics and on the search code; jbell31 had noted in the thread that a Lean proof of this divisibility would close that gap. formal-conjectures records upper bounds and small values of n_k but no general lower bound. The development also proves the Erdős–Selfridge observation and that Cambie's number k · lcm(1, …, k − 1) is admissible, so the lower bound holds for every k ≥ 2 without further assumptions.

records.name: MWIS.Spec.fpt_claim
records.entry_name: An FPT Algorithm for Maximum-Weight Independent Set in Embedded Graphs, in Lean 4
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of a fixed-parameter theorem of "Maximum-weight independent set in embedded graphs parameterized by Euler genus and number of odd faces" (forthcoming), with a provably correct implementation of the algorithm as one fixed program for an explicit sixteen-register pointer machine. Lean proves that for every graph drawn in a closed surface of Euler genus gamma whose complement has k regions of odd total boundary length, and all integer vertex weights, the program outputs a maximum-weight independent set within 2^(c (p size(p) + 1)) (N size(M))^c bit operations, where p = gamma + k, N = |V| + |E| + 1, M = max(1, max |w_v|), size(x) is the binary length of x and c is an absolute constant; that is, 2^O(p log(p+1)) poly(N, log(M+1)) with an absolute polynomial exponent. Surfaces are represented by finite combinatorial flag maps; orientable and nonorientable surfaces, disconnected and noncellular drawings, loops, multiple edges, isolated vertices and negative weights are covered. The algorithm solves one exact linear program per retained component over a finite-group network whose size depends only on p, using exact integral quotient coordinates, midpoint convexity of class minima and a coarse Jensen inequality, and recovers an optimal set from perturbed edge costs. The cost is a logarithmic bit-cost measure including an explicit stack simulation of recursive calls. The proofs use exactly propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: MaderTheorem.mader
records.entry_name: Mader's theorem on highly connected subgraphs
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Mader's 1972 theorem in the form of Diestel's Theorem 1.4.3: for k ≥ 1, every nonempty finite simple graph with average degree at least 4k has a (k + 1)-connected induced subgraph H with e(H)/|H| > e(G)/|G| − k. Vertex connectivity is defined by deletion of fewer than k vertices (same definition as in the Menger–Hamiltonicity entry). Mathlib does not contain vertex connectivity or this theorem.

records.name: SpanningTreeChallenge.maximizer_isoperimetric
records.entry_name: Spanning-Tree Maximization Forces Isoperimetry in the Square Lattice
records.doc: Lean formalization of spanning-tree maximization over finite connected induced subgraphs of the square lattice. The development establishes edge isoperimetry of every maximizer, the maximum count and all maximizing lattice-isometry classes at every positive cardinality, and uniqueness of the canonical corner-strip domain for N >= 18. Nonuniqueness occurs exactly at N = 3, 8, 10, 13; the canonical count has exceptions at N = 7, 14, 17. It also establishes the sharp square-cardinality stability inequality, an exact scalar product formula and rational recurrence for corner-strip counts, the global extremal asymptotic expansion with O(N^(-1/2)) remainder, and the appendix's exact strip-energy Fourier identity, rectangular remainders, Green estimates, and explicit bounds.

records.name: Lavrentieff.extensionDomain_isGδ
records.entry_name: Lavrentieff's Gδ homeomorphism extension theorem
records.doc: Every homeomorphism between arbitrary subsets of completely metrizable spaces extends to a homeomorphism between Gδ supersets contained in the respective closures. Empty subsets and ambient spaces are included. A zero-oscillation construction first gives a Gδ continuous extension domain for maps to complete metric spaces. Restricting the two continuous extensions gives mutually inverse maps. The arbitrary supplied topologies are preserved by compatible complete metrics. Classical mathematics, with no mathematical novelty or priority claim.

records.name: RegularSubgraphTheorem.exists_regular_subgraph
records.entry_name: Regular subgraphs of almost regular graphs (Alon–Friedland–Kalai)
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Alon–Friedland–Kalai theorem for primes: for a prime p, every finite simple graph with maximum degree at most 2p − 1 and average degree greater than 2p − 2 contains a p-regular subgraph (a nonempty subgraph with all degrees 0 or p); as a corollary, every 4-regular graph plus an edge contains a 3-regular subgraph. The prime-power case of the paper is not stated. The proof uses Mathlib's Chevalley–Warning theorem.

records.name: ChangFreimanRuzsa.exists_proper_gap_subset_nsmul_sub_nsmul_dim_le_card_le'
records.entry_name: Chang's version of Freiman's theorem and the Bogolyubov–Ruzsa lemma
records.doc: Formalization of Chang's version of Freiman's theorem, with a 2-proper progression P: a finite set X of integers with |X + X| <= kappa |X| is contained in a 2-proper generalized arithmetic progression of dimension at most the Freiman dimension of X, hence at most 2 kappa - 1, with at most exp(10^32 kappa^7) |X| points. If kappa (2 kappa - 1) <= epsilon |X|, the dimension is at most floor(kappa - 1 + epsilon), as in Green and Tao. There is also a statement for subsets of ZMod q with q prime, where the progression has at most exp(10^30 kappa^7) |X| points. The bound on the size is weaker than that of Chang. The first step of the proof, the Bogolyubov-Ruzsa lemma, is stated too: if moreover |X| >= 7 * 10^7 kappa^2, then 2X - 2X contains a proper progression of dimension at most 3 * 10^5 kappa^2 with at least exp(-2 * 10^7 kappa^2) |X| points.

records.entry_name: Chang's version of Freiman's theorem and the Bogolyubov–Ruzsa lemma
records.doc: Formalization of Chang's version of Freiman's theorem, with a 2-proper progression P: a finite set X of integers with |X + X| <= kappa |X| is contained in a 2-proper generalized arithmetic progression of dimension at most the Freiman dimension of X, hence at most 2 kappa - 1, with at most exp(10^32 kappa^7) |X| points. If kappa (2 kappa - 1) <= epsilon |X|, the dimension is at most floor(kappa - 1 + epsilon), as in Green and Tao. There is also a statement for subsets of ZMod q with q prime, where the progression has at most exp(10^30 kappa^7) |X| points. The bound on the size is weaker than that of Chang. The first step of the proof, the Bogolyubov-Ruzsa lemma, is stated too: if moreover |X| >= 7 * 10^7 kappa^2, then 2X - 2X contains a proper progression of dimension at most 3 * 10^5 kappa^2 with at least exp(-2 * 10^7 kappa^2) |X| points.

records.name: SuperpermutationUpper.finite_bound
records.entry_name: A smaller upper bound for superpermutations
records.doc: For the shortest superpermutation length S(n), construct covering words with asymptotic bound S(n) <= n! + (n-1)! + (n-2)! + (926683/1814400 + o(1))(n-3)!. The development proves an explicit finite bound for every n >= 14 and its numerical consequences. The coefficient is approximately 0.510738. The argument combines a finite selection, a verified connector cover, and transport to larger alphabets.

records.name: SlowEquilibrationCondensedSource.theorem_1_2
records.entry_name: Slow Equilibration and Persistent Stationary Correlations in Spherical Spin Glasses
records.doc: Lean formalization of the six headline result groups: Theorem 1.2, Corollary 1.3, and Theorems 1.4–1.7. Theorem 1.2, Corollary 1.3, and the asymptotic clauses of Theorem 1.4 are conditional only on Chen’s finite-mixture Parisi formula. Universal pressure lower tails are proved internally. The finite-dimensional Haar comparison and Theorems 1.5–1.7 have no literature premise. The manuscript and exact model assumptions are included.

records.name: VerifiedPaper.t01
records.entry_name: A proof of Kroó’s conjecture
records.doc: For every origin-symmetric convex body with nonempty interior in a finite-dimensional real Euclidean space, continuous real boundary functions admit uniform approximation by real homogeneous polynomials of consecutive degrees. The development proves all thirteen principal results of the cited manuscript, including parity approximation, dimension-only uniform approximation of the constant function, homogeneous Gaussian kernels with polynomially weighted errors, fixed-bandwidth one-sided weighted density, tensor density, Gaussian Fourier cutoff, convex weighted approximation, finite-family selection and positive spherical quadrature. The thirteen declarations and their conjunction are compared against an independent self-contained Challenge using only the standard three Lean axioms.

records.name: SuperpermutationPalomar.GeneralLower.exact_word_bound
records.entry_name: Chain returns and lower bounds for superpermutations
records.doc: Prove explicit general lower bounds for the shortest superpermutation length S(n), valid for every n >= 8. The exact-order and quadratic-order formulas refine the lower-order terms while retaining leading correction (2+o(1))(n-4)! above n!+(n-1)!+(n-2)!. The development also proves asymptotic comparisons with earlier general formulas; the selected theorem statements specify their exact scope. Separate finite refinements prove S(10) >= 4033379 and S(14) >= 93891141150.

records.name: OEISProofs.HannaFamily.existsUnique
records.entry_name: Proofs and corrections of OEIS conjectures
records.doc: Machine-checked proofs of conjectures recorded in 29 entries of the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences (OEIS), together with corrections of the four conjectured statements that turn out to be false. Most of the sequences are coefficients of formal power series defined by functional equations, and most of the results describe their residues modulo small integers. The results form six families and a group of further results: the equation A(x*A - m*x*A^2) = x^2 (parity, residues modulo m^2, binary-digit divisibility and prime exponents for every m, with corrected residue classifications modulo 9 and 16 for A396843 and A396844); consecutive iterates F = x + F^{o r}*F^{o(r+1)} (every integer iterate modulo 2r, A396099, A396798, A396807); scaled inverses A(x - x*A(qx)/q) = x (every coefficient is 1 modulo q+1, and for even q the odd coefficients are exactly at the powers of 2, A393856-A393859); theta-series substitutions and theta-type sums (square patterns modulo 4, corrected for A380680, and a congruence modulo 16 for A355872); Catalan-type equations (residues modulo 2, 4 and 8 governed by powers of 2, A393172, A393171, A389536, A397588, A195194); equations with an exact halving step (residues modulo 4, 9 and 3, A389537, A389542, A389474, A389475); and further results on A396093, A392210, A396102 and its family F^{o r} = (1+x)*F^{o(r-1)}, A380056, A397346 and the greedy sequence A394576. Each family has its own Comparator configuration, and each OEIS entry has a self-contained paper in the repository.

records.name: DirectedCycles.nearly_linear_directed_cycles
records.entry_name: Nearly linear directed cycles in vertex-transitive digraphs
records.doc: Formalization of the near-linear directed-cycle theorem: for every real epsilon greater than zero, all sufficiently large finite connected vertex-transitive loopless digraphs on n vertices contain a simple directed cycle of length at least n^(1-epsilon). Connectedness means connectedness of the underlying undirected graph; cycles of length two are allowed. This is Theorem 1.5 of the archived revised manuscript by Bowen Li and Abhishek Methuku, with repaired arguments and replacement lemmas in its proof dependencies. It does not assert Hamiltonicity.

records.name: LeanLab.DensityGoldbach.U1502.alsetriShao_1_2
records.entry_name: A density version of the binary Goldbach problem, after Alsetri and Shao
records.doc: A sorry-free Lean 4 proof, with no cited hypothesis, of Theorem 1.2 of A. Alsetri and X. Shao, Density versions of the binary Goldbach problem, arXiv 2405.18576v2, Acta Arith. 218, 2025, 285 to 295: if A is a set of primes whose relative lower density in every reduced residue class b mod W is at least some eta > 1/2, then almost all even positive integers are a sum of two primes from A. The entry also proves the paper's Theorem 1.1, that relative density 1 - epsilon in the primes alone does not suffice, and the sharpness of the constant 1/2 stated in its Remark 1.3. A derived result of this entry, not a result of the paper, shows that the hypothesis of Theorem 1.2 holds for the set of all primes, so the theorem is not vacuous. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed; Theorem 1.2 concerns almost all even numbers. An AI agent wrote the Lean code, except the ported PrimeNumberTheoremAnd code credited to its authors; the statements were checked against the paper by an AI agent and are offered for human audit.

records.name: C4.conj_sharp
records.entry_name: The optimal Hessian bound for convex four-body central configurations
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Conjecture 7.3 of arXiv:2609.35632 on the central configurations of the planar Newtonian four-body problem. At every strictly convex central configuration of four positive masses, the Hessian form Q of U + (λ/2)I is at least two thirds of its radial part K, and strictly so wherever K is positive. In the notation of the paper this is λ_max(G) < 1/3 for the explicit 2×2 matrix G of its Proposition 3.5, and by its Proposition 7.2 the constant 2/3 is optimal. It sharpens Theorem B of the paper, Q ≥ K/4. The definitions and the reduction to the normal form of Corbera, Cors and Roberts are those of the registered development lean4body-uniqueness. The new parts are a majorant that pays only the largest eigenvalue of S(y), an exact test that is positive definite exactly when λ_max(G) < 1/3, and a computer-assisted proof of that test: a branch and bound with interval arithmetic over the three-dimensional set of normalized convex central configurations, reduced by a symmetry to half of it, and an exact Taylor-form theorem at the corner where the margin of the test vanishes. Lean's kernel checks the certificates with `decide +kernel`. The trusted base is Lean's kernel, including its built-in arithmetic on natural-number literals (GMP-accelerated), and the proofs use only Lean's three standard axioms.

records.name: UCPlanarAudit.counterexample
records.entry_name: Unique-Continuation-Planar
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of every theorem, lemma and proposition of "Unique continuation on planar graphs" (Bou-Rabee, Cooperman and Ganguly): a harmonic function on a periodic plane graph with periodic conductances that is bounded by one on a set of density at least 1 - epsilon is constant (Theorem 1.1), together with the exponential upper bound (Theorem 1.2), the zero case (Theorem 1.3), the topological lemma, the exponential lower bound of the appendix with its polynomial approximation lemma and three-ball proposition, and non-planar periodic conductances on Z^2 with a harmonic function supported on a diagonal (Theorem 5.1).  Three results the paper cites from the literature (Janiszewski's theorem at a point, unicoherence of the sphere and the discrete Moser estimate) are explicit hypotheses of the theorems that use them; the classical Liouville theorem for periodic networks and the discrete Remez inequality are proved. The four main theorems are independently checked using the UCPlanarAudit/ comparator pairs.

records.name: ORRWAudit.range_lower_bound
records.entry_name: ORRW-Lower-Bound
records.doc: A Lean formalization of the paper "Once-reinforced random walk on Z^d has range exponent at least d/(d+1)" by Bou-Rabee and Peres: for d >= 2 and reinforcement beta >= 1, the expected range of once-reinforced random walk is at least c beta^(-d/(d+1)) n^(d/(d+1)) (Theorem 1.1), with a stretched-exponential lower tail (Theorem 1.2), the almost-sure bound it implies, and a bound on the occupation measure (Theorem 1.3). Every lemma and proposition behind them is formalized as well, and nothing is assumed. The four main theorems are independently checked using the ORRWAudit/ comparator pairs.

records.name: DimRed.StatementAudit.DimensionalReduction.dimensional_reduction
records.entry_name: Dynamic dimensional reduction in the Abelian sandpile
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the paper "Dynamic dimensional reduction in the Abelian sandpile" by Bou-Rabee (Comm. Math. Phys. 390 (2022); arXiv:2009.05968), in a corrected edition of the arXiv source: dimensional reduction and self-similarity of the parallel toppling odometer (Theorem 1.1), the corresponding statements for the sandpile (Corollary 1.1) and the regularity proposition (Proposition 4.1) proved with them by one joint induction over dimension, side length and time, together with every lemma, corollary and proposition of Sections 2 and 3. The main results are stated as published. The four Mathlib-only comparator pairs under DimRedAudit/ check Theorem 1.1, Corollary 1.1 and Proposition 4.1.

records.name: TheoremAChallenge.theoremA
records.entry_name: Regularity structures and dynamical Phi^4_3
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the local well-posedness and convergence of the renormalised dynamical Phi^4_3 model on the three-dimensional torus, after Hairer's Theorem 1.15. For smooth initial data, explicit renormalisation constants built from the massive heat kernel, and every exponent eta in (-2/3, -1/2), the solutions of the equation driven by mollified space-time white noise converge in probability in the Hölder–Besov space C^eta up to the maximal existence time of the limit, and the limit does not depend on the mollifier. A standalone library proves the general theory used: the reconstruction theorem (Hairer, Theorem 3.10; Hoshino, Theorem 4.1), weighted reconstruction, the multilevel Schauder estimate (Hairer, Theorem 5.12), maximal solutions, and Malliavin calculus for white noise.

records.name: SpherePackingsAudit.theoremA
records.entry_name: Random walk on sphere packings and Delaunay triangulations in arbitrary dimension
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the paper "Random walk on sphere packings and Delaunay triangulations in arbitrary dimension" by Bou-Rabee and Gwynne: on orthogonal tilings with small mesh and one of three regularity hypotheses, the stopped conductance-weighted random walk converges to stopped Brownian motion modulo time parametrization (Theorem A) and the discrete Dirichlet problem converges (Theorem B, both alternatives); Poisson-Voronoi tessellations satisfy the hypotheses (Proposition 1.1); and simple random walk on a bounded-degree sphere packing need not converge (Theorem 6.1); for any nearest-neighbour walks under Assumption D the stopped walk converges to stopped Brownian motion (Theorem 4.1). Every labelled result is registered and proved, as printed or as in the corrected paper (paper/rw-spheres-corrected.tex), where the printed statement is false, not well defined, or changed with the published version open (README.md); Lemma 5.1(b) is registered with dimension-dependent constants, which is weaker than the printed statement in dimensions 4 to 12, where the printed radius also holds but is not needed. Theorem A and Theorem B(a) are Leonardo Bonanno's (leobon12) formalization, imported with attribution.

records.name: KMV.main_result
records.entry_name: Independent sets in hypergraphs with no loose triangle
records.doc: Conditional Lean formalisation of “Independent sets in hypergraphs with no loose triangle” by Ayush Basu, Abhishek Dhawan and Abhishek Methuku. Assuming the explicitly stated normalized Li–Postle vertex-coloring bound for triangle-free hypergraphs with edges of sizes 3 and 4, for every fixed integer r >= 3 there are constants c > 0 and N such that every n-vertex hypergraph with n >= N, edge sizes between 3 and r, and no loose triangle has an independent set of size at least c n^(2/3) (log log n)^(1/3). The implication is proved in Lean; the Li–Postle premise and the manuscript's Ramsey corollary are not proved in this development.

records.name: PierceLengthBound.P_le_polar_optimal
records.entry_name: Bounds for the iteration x ↦ a mod x
records.doc: For integers 0 < b < a, let P(a,b) count the positive terms obtained by repeatedly replacing x by a mod x, starting at b. This development proves the uniform bound P(a,b) ≤ C_ε a^((41301 - 3 sqrt(82849))/137480 + ε) for every ε > 0, including the external coefficient-uniform affine-curve theorem and the effective Hilbert specialisation sieve, and its rational instance 4317/14677. It also proves the exterior-lattice exponents 471/1559 - 6 sqrt(105)/7795 and 153/520, the joint-invariant exponents (1310-sqrt(655))/4365, 2201/7480 and 128/435 and the earlier exponents 45/152, 8/27, 11/37, 23/77, and 3/10. It also proves a bound O(a^(1/4) sqrt R), where R minus one counts rises in the quotient increments, and positivity and integrality of the orbit's Hankel invariants. A separate conditional theorem gives O(a^(3/10) sqrt(log log(3a))) assuming two explicitly stated analytic estimates whose proofs are not formalised. The polar bound uses the proved orbit identity, actual common-base bound of four, degree-twelve residue labels, uniform arithmetic specialisation count, and full-pattern completion count with arbitrary common divisors. These establish the six-term local estimate without additional hypotheses. The conjectured O((log a)^2) bound remains open.

records.name: BandParity.matching
records.entry_name: BandParity: the band-parity sum of a quartic character, two laws modulo 4
records.doc: For a prime p = 5 (mod 8) let chi be the quartic Dirichlet character with chi(2) = i, with values in the Gaussian integers, and let C(p) = f + i e be the sum of chi(n) (-1)^floor(n^2/p) over 0 < n < p/2. The development proves that f = (p-1)/4 (mod 4) and e = kappa (mod 4) for every such p, where kappa is the sum of the Legendre symbols (n/p) over 0 < n < p/4. The mechanism is a matching lemma: for sign functions sigma, tau and a bijection pi, the correlation sum sigma(x) tau(pi x) is congruent modulo 4 to the sum of the two marginals minus the number of terms, so it does not depend on pi. records.entry_name: BandParity: the band-parity sum of a quartic character, two laws modulo 4
records.doc: For a prime p = 5 (mod 8) let chi be the quartic Dirichlet character with chi(2) = i, with values in the Gaussian integers, and let C(p) = f + i e be the sum of chi(n) (-1)^floor(n^2/p) over 0 < n < p/2. The development proves that f = (p-1)/4 (mod 4) and e = kappa (mod 4) for every such p, where kappa is the sum of the Legendre symbols (n/p) over 0 < n < p/4. records.name: AlgebraicHodgePilot.exists_closed_representative
records.entry_name: Algebraic E1 degeneration from explicit d′d″ identities
records.doc: For actual commuting integer-indexed double complexes over a field, componentwise image/kernel identities imply biclosed representatives of vertical cohomology classes and vanishing of every higher differential of the column-filtered signed total complex. The genuine first quotient page identifies with vertical cohomology; canonical recurrence agrees on actual representatives and covers all next-page classes. Finite rectangular support gives actual quotient stabilization and a canonical identification with the associated graded of total cohomology with its finite, exhaustive, separated induced filtration. Classical conditional algebraic mathematics; no analytic compact-Kähler theorem or novelty claim.

records.name: Erdos699.erdos_699.variants.of_sq_lt
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem 699: every counterexample has n ≤ j²
records.doc: Erdős Problem 699 (Erdős and Szekeres 1978) asks whether for every 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n/2 there is a prime p ≥ i dividing gcd(C(n, i), C(n, j)). The problem is open. Using the statement from google-deepmind/formal-conjectures with the single extra hypothesis j² < n, this project proves in Lean 4 with Mathlib that the answer is yes whenever j² < n; equivalently, every counterexample (n, i, j) has n ≤ j². The proof combines the Erdős–Szekeres inequality gcd(C(n, i), C(n, j)) ≥ C(n, i)/C(j, i) ≥ (n/j)^i, which follows from the identity C(n, j) C(j, i) = C(n, i) C(n − i, j − i), with an upper bound for a gcd whose prime factors are all below i: each prime power in C(n, i) is at most n (Kummer), and there are at most i/2 primes below i, so such a gcd is at most n^(i/2). The bound reduces the problem to j ≥ √n. With a computer search of every n < 10^12 (not part of this formalization) it rules out counterexamples with j ≤ 10^6. The argument is short and may well be folklore; formal-conjectures records the problem but no partial result of this kind.

records.name: RealPowerCauchySchwarz.conjecture_5_1
records.entry_name: A Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for real powers: proof, equality cases and weighted forms
records.doc: For a vector v with nonnegative entries and a real number p, write v^p for the vector of p-th powers of its entries. Johnston, Plosker, Torrance and Varona (arXiv:2507.10327, Conjecture 5.1) conjectured that ‖v^p‖ ‖w^p‖ - ⟨v^p, w^p⟩ ≤ ‖v‖^p ‖w‖^p - ⟨v, w⟩^p for every real p ≥ 2 and all vectors v, w in ℝⁿ with positive entries, with the Euclidean norm and inner product. They proved it for integer p and showed that it fails for 1 < p < 2. This formalization proves the conjecture for every real p ≥ 2 and all vectors with nonnegative entries. It also determines every case of equality: for p > 2 equality holds exactly when v and w are linearly dependent or each has at most one nonzero entry, and for p = 2 there is one further family supported on two coordinates. Finally, for positive coordinate weights ω used in every norm and inner product, the weighted inequality holds for all nonnegative vectors exactly when ω_i ω_j ≥ 1 for all i ≠ j, a condition that does not depend on p. The proof shows that a 2 × 2 entrywise-power defect matrix is positive semidefinite, using a double integral formula and the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for integrals. The conjecture and its equality cases were also proved, independently and concurrently, by Johnston and Sababheh (arXiv:2610.12063).

records.name: KurzPolyhex.volume_hexagon
records.entry_name: Kurz's conjecture on the maximum area of the convex hull of a polyhex
records.doc: A polyhex is an edge-to-edge connected system of cells of the regular hexagonal tiling. Kurz (Convex hulls of polyominoes, Beiträge Algebra Geom. 49 (2008), Conjecture 2) conjectured that the convex hull of a polyhex with n cells of unit area has area at most ⌊n² + 14n/3 + 1⌋ / 6. This formalization proves the conjecture, and the sharper bound ⌈n² + 14n/3⌉ / 6, which differs from Kurz's bound by 1/6 when 3 divides n and agrees with it otherwise. The statements are made in the Euclidean plane for the regular hexagonal tiling, with area measured in units of one cell. The proof writes the hull as the hull of the cell centres plus one hexagon, bounds its area through the area of the centre hull and three of its widths, and controls both with a spanning tree of the polyhex. The accompanying paper (arXiv:2609.30310) also shows that the sharp bound is attained for every n by a path made of three straight runs, so that it is the exact maximum. That construction is not formalized.

records.name: AlmostStacked.G9_connected
records.entry_name: The critical Almost Stacked Hypothesis fails on a nine-vertex graph
records.doc: In graph pebbling, a move removes two pebbles from a vertex and adds one to a neighbour; a configuration is stackable if moves can bring all pebbles onto one vertex and clearable if moves can leave exactly one pebble. The stacking (clearing) number of a connected (connected non-bipartite) graph is the least t >= 2 such that every configuration of t pebbles is stackable (clearable). The Almost Stacked Hypothesis, in its critical form, says that this number equals the least t0 >= 2 such that every almost stacked configuration (one vertex arbitrary, every other vertex at most one pebble) of every size at least t0 is stackable (clearable). We formalise a counterexample to both clauses: on the nine-vertex graph G9 (graph6 HCQTaXi) the stacking and clearing numbers are 15, the only non-stackable and non-clearable configurations of size 14 are (0,0,1,0,0,5,0,8,0) and its automorphic image, neither almost stacked, while every almost stacked configuration of size at least 14 is stackable and clearable. Hence neither clause holds for all finite connected (respectively connected non-bipartite) graphs. The finite facts are proved by kernel evaluation (decide +kernel) of a verified exact losing-layer checker on certificate data; general lemmas (clearable implies stackable; monotonicity above the order) are proved by hand.

records.name: PolytopeTrees.U_recurrence
records.entry_name: The Number of Polytope Trees and Beyond — Lean 4 formalization
records.doc: Symmetry-weighted enumeration of finite facet-pairing diagrams and polytope trees: cut-join recurrences, factorial formulas, formal exponential generating functions, local analytic counting series with specified radical branches, binomial identities and asymptotic equivalents. The development also proves unique extension of intrinsic facet isometries for finite spanning flag-regular Euclidean cells, derives their geometric presentation masses, and proves an exponential lower bound for ordinary simplicial triangulation classes from any fixed finite pure triangulation of dimension at least two.

records.doc: Symmetry-weighted enumeration of finite facet-pairing diagrams and polytope trees: cut-join recurrences, factorial formulas, formal exponential generating functions, local analytic counting series with specified radical branches, binomial identities and asymptotic equivalents. The development also proves unique extension of intrinsic facet isometries for finite spanning flag-regular Euclidean cells, derives their geometric presentation masses, and proves an exponential lower bound for ordinary simplicial triangulation classes from any fixed finite pure triangulation of dimension at least two.

records.name: ArtGallery.etrinv_erComplete
records.entry_name: The Art Gallery Problem is ∃ℝ-complete: point-point, boundary-point and point-boundary variants, in Lean 4
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Abrahamsen, Adamaszek and Miltzow, "The Art Gallery Problem is ∃ℝ-complete" (J. ACM 2021), together with Stade's point-boundary variant (SoCG 2025), for an explicit single-tape Turing machine model. Lean proves that deciding whether a simple polygon with rational corners can be guarded by g guards is ∃ℝ-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions in each of the three variants known to be ∃ℝ-complete: point guards guarding the whole polygon (Theorem 1, also for integer corners), guards on the boundary guarding the whole polygon (the boundary-point variant of the paper's §7.2), and point guards guarding only the boundary (Stade's theorem); that ETR-INV is ∃ℝ-complete; that the guard sets of the paper's Section 5 polygon correspond exactly to the solutions of an ETR-INV instance (Theorem 54, with the range condition made explicit) and encode the solutions of any ETR formula (Theorem 55); that every real algebraic number is the x-coordinate of a guard in every optimal guard set of some polygon with rational corners (Theorem 2); and that some x-monotone polygon with integer corners can be guarded by three guards but needs four rational guards (Theorem 4). The development provides reusable material on the existential theory of the reals: formulas and their codes, the class ∃ℝ, ETR-INV and ETR-INV-REV with polynomial-time reductions from ETR, and an elementary proof of the doubly exponential solution bound that the paper cites from Schaefer and Štefankovič. It partially answers the open problem of the paper's §7.2 on the number of variables: all three art gallery problems reduce to ETR by formulas whose only variables are the 2g coordinates of the guards (the paper uses (n+g)^6 variables for n corners). Point-point and point-boundary hardness is proved through Stade's construction; the paper's own Section 5 construction is formalized for Theorems 54 and 55, with gadget visibility facts checked as kernel-evaluated certificates, and a modification of it (guard segments on shallow bays in the boundary, re-laid-out addition gadgets) gives boundary-point hardness. The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

Lean proves that deciding whether a simple polygon with rational corners can be guarded by g guards is ∃ℝ-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions in each of the three variants known to be ∃ℝ-complete: point guards guarding the whole polygon (Theorem 1, also for integer corners), guards on the boundary guarding the whole polygon (the boundary-point variant of the paper's §7.2), and point guards guarding only the boundary (Stade's theorem); that ETR-INV is ∃ℝ-complete; that the guard sets of the paper's Section 5 polygon correspond exactly to the solutions of an ETR-INV instance (Theorem 54, with the range condition made explicit) and encode the solutions of any ETR formula (Theorem 55); that every real algebraic number is the x-coordinate of a guard in every optimal guard set of some polygon with rational corners (Theorem 2); and that some x-monotone polygon with integer corners can be guarded by three guards but needs four rational guards (Theorem 4). Point-point and point-boundary hardness is proved through Stade's construction; the paper's own Section 5 construction is formalized for Theorems 54 and 55, with gadget visibility facts checked as kernel-evaluated certificates, and a modification of it (guard segments on shallow bays in the boundary, re-laid-out addition gadgets) gives boundary-point hardness. records.name: birthday_paradox
records.entry_name: birthday-paradox-non-backtracking-regular-graphs
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization (found by Codex GPT 5.6 Sol) of the main theorem of the author's recent arxiv preprint	arXiv:2608.26321.  This is the Birthday Paradox for non-backtracking walks on regular graphs of degree at least 3: such a walk of length k has high probability of self-intersecting when k is significantly greater than sqrt(n), where n is the number of vertices of the graph. This resolves a conjecture of Noga Alon and Yuval Peres for the fixed degree case.

records.name: PureTypeSystem.weak_implies_strong_betaEta
records.entry_name: Weak and strong βη-normalization in pure type systems with βη-conversion
records.doc: A Lean formalization of the Barendregt-Geuvers-Klop conjecture, "weak normalization implies strong normalization", for the pure type systems PTS_βη of Geuvers (Logics and Type Systems, 1993), whose conversion rule uses βη-conversion. For every PTS specification, with no functionality assumption, it proves two theorems about the legal terms of PTS_βη. If every legal term is weakly βη-normalizing, then every legal term is strongly βη-normalizing. If every legal term is weakly β-normalizing, then every legal term is strongly βη-normalizing. The proof adapts OpenAI's 2026 proof of the β case for PTS_β, whose Lean files are included. An η-step can delete a λ-annotation, so the proof works from a weaker hypothesis, that every legal term has a β-reduct with no β-redex outside its λ-domains. Conversion is handled through domain erasure, candidates are indexed by βη-normal forms of erased types, and observation values are made η-canonical.

records.name: challenge_main_smallest
records.entry_name: Perron's extremal solutions of the Bernoulli one-phase problem: viscosity, inner variational and one-sided minimizing solutions, and free boundary structure in the plane
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the main results of Abedin, Feldman and Stinson on Perron's extremal solutions of the one-phase Bernoulli free boundary problem Δu = 0 in {u > 0} ∩ U, |∇u| = Q on ∂{u > 0} ∩ U. Let U ⊂ ℝᵈ, d ≥ 2, be open, bounded and connected with C² boundary, and let Q be Lipschitz on the closure of U with 0 < Q_min ≤ Q ≤ Q_max. Theorem 1.1: the smallest supersolution above a smooth strict subsolution g with g > 0 on ∂U is (i) a viscosity solution in U, (ii) an inner variational solution in U for some χ (the first domain variation of the Alt–Caffarelli energy ∫ |∇u|² + Q² χ vanishes), and (iii) a downward minimizer of that energy on a ball around each free boundary point; the largest subsolution below a smooth strict supersolution g has the same three properties, with upward minimality in (iii). Corollary 1.2, in ℝ²: (i) the free boundary of the smallest supersolution is the disjoint union of a relatively open set, near each point of which u is a classical solution (a C^{1,γ} free boundary, u harmonic in {u > 0}, ∇u continuous up to the free boundary with |∇u| = Q there), and a set at each point x₀ of which every blow-up limit of u is the two-plane function Q(x₀)|y · e| for some unit vector e; (ii) the largest subsolution is a classical solution near every free boundary point. Every notion, including viscosity solutions, smooth strict sub- and supersolutions, Perron's classes, inner variational solutions, Sobolev functions, the one-sided minimizers, blow-up limits and classical solutions, is written out from Mathlib definitions. A fifth statement is the necklace example, a rigorous version, with different parameters, of the numerical example in Figure 1 of the paper: in ℝ² with Q ≡ 1 there are a domain and data, with the same boundary values for both problems, whose smallest supersolution and largest subsolution are both nontrivial and differ on a set of positive measure, the smallest supersolution has a two-plane point, and a minimizer of the Alt–Caffarelli energy with the same boundary data exists and differs from both extremal solutions on sets of positive measure. It also shows that the hypotheses of the other statements can be met and that their conclusions are not degenerate.

records.name: SteklovSubmission.main_result
records.entry_name: Strictly Convex Steklov-Isospectral Plane Domains
records.doc: Formalization of a family of pairs of bounded, simply connected, strictly convex planar domains with real-analytic boundaries. At each parameter, the two domains have identical Steklov spectra, including multiplicities. Distinct labels or parameters give noncongruent domains. Each domain has perimeter 2π and no orientation-reversing Euclidean symmetry, and normalized conformal maps converge in C∞ to the identity. The proof uses an explicit degree-seven construction.

records.name: BernoulliCertificate.unequal_finite_bernoulli_shifts
records.entry_name: Finite uniform Bernoulli shifts with unequal base entropy
records.doc: There exist a countable group G and a nontrivial finite alphabet A such that the ordinary left Bernoulli shifts on A and A times A, equipped with their uniform product probability measures, are equivariantly measure-preservingly isomorphic on invariant conull measurable sets. The inverse is measurable. The finite alphabets have different cardinalities and therefore different uniform base Shannon entropies. The algebraic existence input is supplied by the pinned OpenAI proofs. This formalization does not certify all-base collapse, finitary continuity, the integer coding inputs, or the manuscript's later corollaries.

records.name: HiltonMilnerTheorem.hilton_milner
records.entry_name: The Hilton–Milner theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Hilton–Milner theorem: for k ≥ 2 and n > 2k, a nontrivial intersecting family of k-subsets of an n-set (no element lies in all members) has at most C(n−1, k−1) − C(n−k−1, k−1) + 1 members, and this bound is attained. Intersecting is Mathlib's Set.Intersecting. Mathlib contains the Erdős–Ko–Rado theorem but not this result.

records.name: LeanLab.Routes.U1508.goldbach_445_hsw_gZ
records.entry_name: CONDITIONAL on RH and cited zero counts: Goldbach numbers in intervals of length 4.45 log^2 x
records.doc: CONDITIONAL. A Lean 4 proof that, under the Riemann Hypothesis, for every real x at least 3 there is a Goldbach number n, a sum of two odd primes, with x < n < x + 4.45 (log x)^2. This improves the constant 123 of A. Chirre and M. V. Hagen, On Goldbach numbers in short intervals, arXiv 2512.23534, by their method. RH is the paper's own hypothesis. The theorem is CONDITIONAL ON seven cited inputs taken as explicit hypotheses, never as axioms, all stated for gZ, the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function counted with multiplicity: ExplicitA, the truncated explicit formula of Montgomery and Vaughan, Multiplicative Number Theory I, display 12.1, under RH; HadamardK, the bound sum over gamma' of 4/(4 + (gamma - gamma')^2) at most log |gamma|, a consequence of the Hadamard product, under RH; Ordinates14, every ordinate at least 14 in absolute value; BPTN, the zero count of Brent, Platt and Trudgian, J. Number Theory 238, 2022, Lemma 1, for T at least 10^13; HSWN70 and HSWHead14, the zero count of Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong, arXiv 2107.06506, Corollary 1.2, for T at least 70 and T at least 14; and EvenGoldbachUpTo 4*10^18, the verification of the even Goldbach conjecture to 4*10^18 by Oliveira e Silva, Herzog and Pardi, Math. Comp. 83, 2014. These are the Lean Lab's transcriptions, not Mathlib results. Everything else in the argument is proved: Theorem 2 of Chirre and Hagen with the diagonal constant lowered to 1.0068, the passage from psi to theta, and their Section 5. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. An AI agent, Claude, wrote the Lean code, with the ported PrimeNumberTheoremAnd files credited to their authors in PORTING.md; the statements were checked against the papers by AI agents and are offered for human audit.

records.name: KirkmanTheorem.kirkman
records.entry_name: Kirkman's theorem on Steiner triple systems
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Kirkman's 1847 theorem: for v ≥ 1, a Steiner triple system on v points (a family of 3-subsets covering every pair of distinct points exactly once) exists if and only if v ≡ 1 or 3 (mod 6). Sufficiency is proved by Bose's and Skolem's constructions from Steiner quasigroups. Mathlib does not contain Steiner triple systems.

records.name: NashWilliamsOrientation.nash_williams
records.entry_name: Nash-Williams' weak orientation theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Nash-Williams' weak orientation theorem (1960): every 2k-edge-connected finite graph has a k-arc-connected orientation, i.e. one in which every nonempty proper vertex set is left by at least k arcs. It is proved for finite loopless multigraphs given by an edge family, and stated for simple graphs with Mathlib's SimpleGraph.IsEdgeConnected and orientations as Mathlib Digraphs. The proof is by induction on the number of edges, with Mader's lemma (a minimally 2k-edge-connected multigraph has a vertex of degree 2k) and Lovász's splitting lemma, both proved in the project. Mathlib does not contain these results.

records.name: KnasterReichbach.exists_homeomorph_extension
records.entry_name: Knaster–Reichbach homeomorphism extension on Cantor space
records.doc: Every homeomorphism between closed nowhere-dense subsets of Cantor space extends to a homeomorphism of the entire Cantor space, with exact pointwise agreement. Cantor space is the usual product topology on Nat -> Bool. Empty prescribed subsets are included. The proof constructs matched finite clopen refinements by alternating binary coordinate splits, then obtains mutually inverse continuous limit maps. Classical result; no novelty or priority claim.

records.name: CantorDynamics.exists_extension_dense_forward_orbit
records.entry_name: Cantor dynamical extension with a dense forward orbit
records.doc: Every homeomorphism of a closed nowhere-dense subset A of the usual Cantor space Nat -> Bool extends pointwise to an ambient homeomorphism H with a dense forward orbit. Empty A is included. The proof constructs an orbit embedding into the two-sided full shift, extends it using Knaster–Reichbach, proves forward shift orbit density by finite-coordinate patching and Baire, and conjugates back. Classical invariant-subset case only; no novelty claim.

records.name: PalomarEuler.main_result
records.entry_name: Finite-Lp vorticity nonuniqueness for two-dimensional Euler
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of nonuniqueness for the unforced incompressible Euler equations on the two-dimensional square torus. For each finite real exponent p at least one and each positive time interval, the selected theorem constructs a common mean-zero, divergence-free initial datum in L2 and W1p, and two distinct weak solutions continuous in time with values in L2. Their distributional vorticities have strongly measurable Lp-valued representatives that are essentially bounded in time. This is the two-dimensional finite-Lp question in the first part of Buckmaster and Vicol's Problem 6. The full proof and reproducibility checks have passed.

records.name: EdmondsPolytope.edmonds_perfect_matching_polytope
records.entry_name: Edmonds' perfect matching polytope and matching polytope
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Edmonds' theorems (1965) for finite simple graphs: the convex hull of the incidence vectors of the perfect matchings is {x ≥ 0, x(δ(v)) = 1 for every vertex v, x(δ(S)) ≥ 1 for every odd set S}, and the convex hull of the incidence vectors of all matchings is {x ≥ 0, x(δ(v)) ≤ 1, x(E[S]) ≤ (|S| − 1)/2 for every odd S}. Vectors are indexed by the edges of the graph, the convex hull is Mathlib's convexHull, and matchings are Mathlib's Subgraph.IsMatching and Subgraph.IsPerfectMatching. The perfect matching theorem is proved for multigraphs by induction with shrinking of tight odd cuts; the matching polytope follows by the doubling construction. Mathlib does not contain these results.

records.doc: Every nonempty open subset U of a perfect Polish space X contains a closed topological embedding e of Cantor space Nat -> Bool such that every ordered pair of distinct image points lies in each member of a countable family of dense-open subsets R_n of X × X.
