records.name: Z2Z4Rank6.theorem_1_1
records.entry_name: Infinitely many elliptic curves with torsion Z/2Z × Z/4Z and rank at least six
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the paper "Infinitely many elliptic curves with torsion Z/2Z × Z/4Z and rank at least six" by Manvir Jaswal. Theorem 1.1 says that infinitely many elliptic curves over Q have torsion subgroup Z/2Z × Z/4Z and rank at least six, with infinitely many distinct j-invariants. The curves are fibers of a one-parameter family of Dujella and Peral, y² = x(x + a²)(x + b²), which has rank three over Q(m) and gains three further independent points over the function field of a curve C of genus one; congruences carry the independence of the six points, and the torsion, from one rational point of C to infinitely many. Theorem 1.2 shows that the smooth projective model of C is isomorphic over Q to an elliptic curve of conductor 9240 and rank one, that the family has rank exactly six over Q(C), and that at all but finitely many rational points of C its fibers have torsion exactly Z/2Z × Z/4Z and rank at least six. Theorem 8.1 gives a second such family, over a curve of genus one whose Jacobian has rank two. All 19 numbered results of the paper are proved. The theorems take published theorems of other authors as hypotheses, each stated in general form, about no curve or surface of the paper; Theorem 1.1 takes four: Mazur's torsion theorem, the integrality of torsion points at odd primes, that reduction at a prime of good reduction is a homomorphism, and that the points of an elliptic curve over Q_p form a compact topological group. Comparator checks Theorem 1.1; the other results are proved in the same library.

records.name: Critical2DKPZAudit.criticalKPZ_main
records.entry_name: The Critical 2D KPZ Process
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of "The Critical 2D KPZ Process" by Berger, Caravenna, Clark, Dunlap, Gu, Liu, Nakajima, Sun, Tsai, Xie and Zygouras (arXiv:2610.31614, version 1), together with selected inputs and adaptations in the form these proofs need. For directed polymers on Z^2 in a Gaussian environment at critical disorder, it proves the existence of a critical 2D stochastic heat flow, defined as the joint limit in law of the rescaled partition functions (Theorem A). The centred log-partition function converges in law, in the local negative Sobolev spaces H^{-a}_loc and jointly in finitely many times and initial data, to the critical 2D KPZ process (Theorem 1.2). The process satisfies the comparison principle in the initial data. For flat initial data, its averages at scale epsilon, divided by sqrt(log log(1/epsilon)), converge in law to a centred Gaussian (Theorem 1.4(i)); it has a radial covariance kernel equivalent to log log(1/|z|) at the diagonal (Theorem 1.4(ii)), is not a signed measure (Proposition 1.5), is not Gaussian (Theorem 1.6), is invariant under translations and rotations and covariant under scaling (Proposition 1.8), and its pairing with each nonnegative test function has a law of Ehrhard type (Proposition 3.8). It also proves strict skewness, twice differentiable response to initial data, Brownian motion across scales and the finite-dimensional GFF tangent (Theorems A–D of Scott Armstrong’s note). The parameter theta is fixed. Built on Mathlib. All proofs use only Lean's standard axioms.

records.name: Factoring.subexponentialRate
records.entry_name: Deterministic factoring in time N^{o(1)}
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof, against Mathlib, that one deterministic Turing machine computes the smallest prime factor Nat.minFac N of every natural number N in time N^{o(1)}: for every k >= 1 there is a constant C_k such that the same machine halts with the correct output within C_k * 2^(n/k) steps on every n-bit input. The machine model is Mathlib's Turing machine model TM2 (Turing.FinTM2 with Turing.TM2ComputableInTime), with numbers in binary (Computability.encodeNat) and every stack alphabet finite. The best previously published deterministic bounds known to the authors have exponent 1/5 (Harvey 2021; Harvey and Hittmeir 2022). The proof reduces finding the smallest prime factor to counting divisors with prescribed leading bits, expresses that count as the value of a network of local checks carrying out Schoenhage-Strassen multiplication, and evaluates it with a re-proved form of the counting engine of the 2026 3-SAT preprint by Claude (Anthropic). The Challenge also states, as a proposition only and without proof, a conjecture that factoring can be done in time exp(O(log N / sqrt(log log N))). The ideas and the Lean code were generated by AI; the authors audited the statement, not the proof.

records.name: LeanLab.BS2022GRH.Cert1575.chenThreshold13375_of_deep_closed
records.entry_name: An explicit version of Chen's theorem assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof, conditional on the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis and on four cited results, that every even integer N at least e^{e^{13.375}} is the sum of a prime and a square-free number greater than 1 with at most two prime factors. The four cited inputs are explicit hypotheses of the theorem, never axioms: Thm5J, Thm6J and Thm7J, the Lean Lab's transcriptions of Theorems 5, 6 and 7 of M. Bordignon and V. Starichkova, An explicit version of Chen's theorem assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, Ramanujan J. 64, 2024, 1213 to 1242; and LinearSieveT4 1/8349 112 114, the transcription of their Theorem 4, the explicit linear sieve of Bordignon, Johnston and Starichkova with the Table 1 row epsilon inverse 6100, C1 = 112, C2 = 114. In version 2 each of Thm5J, Thm6J and Thm7J also takes 0 <= C1 and 0 <= C2 as premises right after the sieve hypothesis, matching Table 1, which lists positive constants only. These transcriptions use the Lean normalisation U_N = 2 e^{-gamma} C2 Pi_N, twice the U_N printed in the journal; see the fidelity section. GRH for Dirichlet L-functions is the premise inside the conclusion ChenThreshold13375. The journal's own Corollary 1 has the threshold e^{e^{14}}; the threshold e^{e^{13.375}} comes from re-choosing the Section 5.4 parameters inside the authors' method, alpha = 0.00256, A = 10, u = 1500, epsilon = 1/8349, epsilon1 = 10^-20. The numeric inputs are proved here: epsilon at 1500 is below 1/8349 by a kernel certificate, decide +kernel in eleven window modules, and the Section 5.4 bracket combination is at least the main-term constant minus 10^-5, a one-sided lower bound. Chen's weighted inequality, the journal's Lemma 9, is proved unconditionally. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. An AI agent, Claude, wrote all the Lean code; the statements were checked against the paper by AI agents and are offered for human audit.

records.name: group_constructions_cannot_refute_SCC
records.entry_name: Group constructions cannot refute the Set Cover Conjecture, including tensor powers
records.doc: Pratt (STOC 2024, arXiv:2311.02774, Corollary 1.12) showed that if the Set Cover Conjecture holds, then for every k the asymptotic rank of the balanced tripartitioning tensor T_k is at least tau_k = 8^k * C(3k,k) * C(2k,k) / 27^k. A natural way to bound this rank, and Pratt's own route to rank at most 8^k/2, is a group construction: maps f1, f2, f3 from k-subsets of a 3k-set to a group G with f1(A) f2(B) f3(C) = 1 exactly when A, B, C are pairwise disjoint (a partition analogue of the Cohn-Umans triple product property). We formalise that no such construction, in any finite group, abelian or not, can refute the conjecture: |G| > tau_k for every k >= 2. The same holds for Strassen combinatorial degenerations of group tensors (border-rank constructions), via |G| >= C(3k, floor(3k/2)) > tau_k. The proof formalises a rigidity theorem: the triple products always factor through pairwise commuting elements, f1(A) f2(B) f3(C) = prod_i g_i^(m_i - 1) with m the multiplicity vector, so non-abelian groups give no advantage, unlike in the Cohn-Umans approach to matrix multiplication. It also formalises a lift lemma giving |G| >= 2^(3k-1), which shows Pratt's 8^k/2 is exactly optimal among group restrictions. Pratt's Corollary 1.12 and the passage from a group embedding to a rank bound are cited, not formalised. The bounds concern the group size needed by such constructions, not the rank of T_k itself. Joint constructions for tensor powers are covered: a degeneration of a group tensor onto T_k^(tensor m) needs |G| >= C(3k, floor(3k/2))^m > tau_k^m, so the induced asymptotic-rank bound |G|^(1/m) stays above tau_k.

records.name: PippengerSpencer.pippenger_spencer
records.entry_name: The Pippenger–Spencer theorem on the chromatic index of hypergraphs
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the theorem of Pippenger and Spencer (1989): for r ≥ 2 and ε > 0 there are μ > 0 and D₀ such that every r-uniform hypergraph whose degrees lie in [(1 − μ)D, D] and whose codegrees are at most μD, with D ≥ D₀, has chromatic index at most (1 + ε)D. A second theorem gives an explicit polynomial error: if the maximum degree is at most D, the codegrees are at most D^{1−δ} and there are at most exp(D^γ) edges, then the chromatic index is at most D + D^{1−γ} for some γ = γ(r, δ) > 0. The proofs build on the author's registered formalization of Ehard–Glock–Joos (PALOMAR-2026-10-17-000004): batches of the trimmed Rödl nibble with the Lovász Local Lemma for the first theorem, and the pseudorandom matching theorem (Ehard–Glock–Joos, Theorem 1.2) applied to an auxiliary colour hypergraph for the second. Mathlib does not contain these results.

records.name: ComputationalHodge.period_d0
records.entry_name: Harmonic representatives and period separation for computational-path presentations
records.doc: For finite primitive-step sets in the scoped geometric computational-path model, actual signed trace periods define a cochain complex. Closedness is equivalent to invariance under the entire scoped rewrite relation. Orthogonal projection constructs the unique harmonic representative of every degree-one presentation cohomology class, preserves all loop periods, and induces an actual linear equivalence. Vanishing of all loop periods is equivalent to being a coboundary, without connectivity assumptions; periods separate cohomology and harmonic representatives. A nonzero parallel-edge model and a named-rewrite control expose the distinction from ambient geometric homotopy. Discrete presentation cohomology only, not analytic or Kahler Hodge theory.

records.name: HewittSavage.category_zero_one
records.entry_name: Category Hewitt–Savage zero-one law for infinite Baire products
records.doc: A subset A of X^J with the property of Baire, invariant under every permutation moving only finitely many indices, is meagre or has meagre complement when J is infinite and the actual product space X^J is Baire. A corollary covers countable products of any Polish space. Finite-support displacement, cylinder mixing and the category contradiction are proved, not assumed.

records.name: RandomGraphThresholds.posa
records.entry_name: Hamiltonicity and connectivity thresholds of the random graph G(n, p)
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of two classical threshold results for the binomial random graph G(n, p), modelled as a finite product probability space with one independent Bernoulli(p) coin per pair of vertices: Pósa's theorem (1976) that G(n, p) with p ≥ C log n / n is Hamiltonian with probability tending to 1, also stated with the explicit constant C = 80 (posa_eighty), and both sides of the Erdős–Rényi connectivity threshold (1959): G(n, (log n ± ω(n))/n) with ω(n) → ∞, the edge probability clipped to [0, 1], is connected with probability tending to 1, resp. 0. Hamiltonicity and connectivity are Mathlib's SimpleGraph.IsHamiltonian and SimpleGraph.Connected. Mathlib defines the binomial random graph as a measure on graphs (SimpleGraph.binomialRandom); this project uses its own finite product model instead, and these threshold theorems are not in Mathlib.

records.name: ThreeFlowTheorem.three_flow_of_six_edge_connected
records.entry_name: Nowhere-zero 3-flows in 6-edge-connected graphs
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the theorem of Lovász, Thomassen, Wu and Zhang: every finite 6-edge-connected simple graph has a nowhere-zero integer 3-flow (the weak 3-flow conjecture). The proof formalizes Theorem 3.1 of the paper (β-orientations of multigraphs modulo 3) and Tutte's lifting theorem. Only simple graphs are stated; the paper's multigraph version and its results on modulo k-orientations for k > 3 are not stated. Mathlib does not contain this theorem.

records.name: PlanarChoosability.choosableWith_three_of_isPlanar
records.entry_name: Thomassen: planar graphs of girth at least five are 3-choosable
records.doc: Finite planar simple graphs of extended girth at least five are 3-choosable over arbitrary colour types. Includes a complete six-vertex boundary-extension induction, actual induced-face geometry and residual list-colouring infrastructure. Additional results expose the short-path theorem, derive an infinite finite-list compactness consequence, extend arbitrary five/six-cycles, and extend outer seven-cycles. The full original Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2 are also proved, including arbitrary allowed fixed-edge colours and all exterior components.

Additional results expose the short-path theorem, derive an infinite finite-list compactness consequence, extend arbitrary five/six-cycles, and extend outer seven-cycles. The full original Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2 are also proved, including arbitrary allowed fixed-edge colours and all exterior components.

records.name: NaturalCohomologySteinerPaper.main_result
records.entry_name: Natural cohomology of general Steiner bundles
records.doc: Formalizes Theorem 1.1 of Natural Cohomology of General Steiner Bundles. Over every characteristic-zero field, for all n >= 1, t >= 1, and r >= n, a nonempty principal open of t by (t+r) matrices of linear forms on projective n-space has maximal rank in every homogeneous degree. The transposes give exact Steiner presentations of actual rank-r locally free sheaves, whose integer twists each have at most one nonzero sheaf cohomology group. The coefficient open is nonempty over the original field.

records.name: PDIC.palomar_complete_probability_and_spider
records.entry_name: Zero-Sum Quartet Incidence and Sharp Maximal-Independent-Set Witnesses on Eight Vertices
records.doc: We prove an exact four-term probability law for zero-sum maximal-independent-set witnesses. For every connected simple graph G on eight vertices and every admissible eight-point cap U in F_3^3, sample uniformly from all 40,320 bijections of the vertices onto U. Let N0 count zero-sum maximal independent four-sets, m count the size-four maximal independent sets, n0 and n2 count their unordered pairs intersecting in zero and two vertices, and h count compatible unordered triples. Put M1 = 2m/35, M2 = 2n0/35 + n2/315, and M3 = h/315. Then P(N0=0) = 1-M1+M2-M3, P(N0=1) = M1-2M2+3M3, P(N0=2) = M2-3M3, and P(N0=3) = M3 = h/315 <= 1/105; equality holds if and only if G is isomorphic to the spider S(2,2,2,1). In particular N0 <= 3. The theorem does not assume an external cap normal-form classification.

records.name: LeanLab.Halupczok2012.theorem2Zeroed_U1510
records.entry_name: CONDITIONAL on Perelli-Pintz-Salerno 1984 and Perelli-Pintz 1993: Halupczok's ternary Goldbach mean value theorem with primes in progressions and short intervals, repaired
records.doc: CONDITIONAL on two cited results, both taken as explicit hypotheses of the theorems and never as axioms: PPS1984Remark, the printed Remark on p. 530 of A. Perelli, J. Pintz and S. Salerno, Bombieri's theorem in short intervals, 1984, and PP1993Goldbach, the Goldbach analogue of Theorem 3 of A. Perelli and J. Pintz, On the exceptional set for Goldbach's problem in short intervals, 1993, established in its sections 3 to 5 but not printed as a numbered theorem. These are the inputs that the paper's own proof quotes as its Theorems 2.1 and 2.3. PP1993Goldbach is therefore a weaker citation than a numbered theorem: it is the unnumbered Goldbach analogue that Halupczok says the proof of Perelli and Pintz can be adapted to give, stated here in the general form that argument yields. Under the two hypotheses, a complete Lean 4 proof of a repaired form of Theorem 1.2 of K. Halupczok, Goldbach's problem with primes in arithmetic progressions and in short intervals, J. Theor. Nombres Bordeaux 25, 2013, 331 to 351: summed over moduli q <= Q, the weighted count of p1 + p2 + p3 = n with p1 = a mod q and p1, p2 in short intervals differs from its singular series main term T(n, q, a) Y1 Y2 by << Y1 Y2 L^-A. As printed, the theorem sums over all q <= Q with the printed T, which does not vanish when a and q have a common factor, while the prime sum then is empty, so the printed statement fails, for example at a = 3, q = 3. The repair takes the main term to be 0 for such q, or equivalently restricts to q coprime to a. The entry also proves that the two hypotheses imply the paper's Theorems 2.1 and 2.3, as derived results of this entry. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed; ternary Goldbach is a theorem of Helfgott. An AI agent wrote the Lean code; the statements were checked against the sources by an AI agent and are offered for human audit.

records.name: ErdosPaperI.paperI_main_sharp
records.entry_name: Affine profile reduction for fractional triangle packings in split graphs
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main result of the author's preprint "Affine Profile Reduction for Fractional Triangle Packings in Split Graphs" (Erdős #81 series, Paper I): for every finite split graph G on n vertices, |E(G)| − 2ν₃*(G) ≤ n²/6 + n/2, where ν₃* is the fractional triangle packing number (the maximum total weight of a nonnegative weighting of the triangles with load at most one on every edge). It is stated both for the paper's finite split model (clique Fin p, independent vertices, neighbourhoods) and for every split graph in Mathlib's SimpleGraph, with the definitions of split graphs and fractional triangle packings of two registered entries; the weaker bound n²/6 + n of the first edition is also included. The proof reduces the fractional packing problem to neighbourhood profiles and a three-variable linear program, using finite LP duality. Version 2 states the finite LP duality used in the series as results of its own, over ℝ (Farkas' lemma in inequality form and covering/packing strong duality, from this proof) and over ℚ (Farkas' lemma by Fourier–Motzkin elimination and strong duality for the rational packing LP, from the author's Paper V).

records.name: BaireRegularization.exists_continuous_restriction
records.entry_name: Baire-measurable regularization on comeagre G-delta subspaces
records.doc: For any topological source and second countable target, open inverse images have the property of Baire exactly when the function restricts continuously to some comeagre G-delta subspace. A Baire-source corollary also proves density. The countable basis synchronization and converse relative-open argument are proved internally.

records.name: TsirelsonContractions.Entry.chsh_norm_le_of_contractions
records.entry_name: CHSH bounds for contractions by dilation: Tsirelson's bound, the classical bound under a commuting party, and the necessity of noncommutativity
records.doc: Kernel-checked transfer of the exact CHSH constants for self-adjoint involutions (Mathlib's IsCHSHTuple in a C*-normed ring: the norm of the CHSH operator T = A0 B0 + A0 B1 + A1 B0 - A1 B1 is at most 2*sqrt(2), equals 2 under a commuting party (the equality in a nontrivial real C*-normed algebra; the <= forms in every C*-normed ring), and exceeds 2 only if both parties are noncommuting) to self-adjoint CONTRACTIONS, together with the state corollary. A CHSH contraction tuple is four self-adjoint operators of norm at most 1 with the four cross-party commutations - IsCHSHTuple with the involution relations relaxed to norm bounds. The Challenge imports Mathlib only; the three structures it uses (IsCHSHContractionTuple for matrices, IsDensityMatrix, Hilbert.IsCHSHContractionTuple for operators) are verbatim copies of the library's, checked byte for byte by scripts/check_challenge_definitions.py. The Mathlib definitions the statements import (the scoped l2-operator norm on matrices, PosSemidef under ComplexOrder, IsSelfAdjoint and the adjoint, the trace, the operator norm, WithLp 2, IsCHSHTuple) are quoted verbatim from the pinned source with permalinks in MATHLIB_DEFINITIONS.md and kernel-checked in DefinitionAudit.lean, a default build target that is not compared.

records.name: SpectralIsometry.main_result
records.entry_name: A proof of the spectral isometry conjecture for C*-algebras
records.doc: A formal proof that every unital surjective complex-linear spectral isometry between arbitrary complex unital C*-algebras is an algebraic Jordan isomorphism. The development also proves that a bounded generator whose exponentials are unital spectral isometries at every complex parameter is an associative derivation, and that every surjective spectral isometry is a unital Jordan isomorphism multiplied by its prescribed central unitary value at the identity.

records.name: EZero.finite_flip_mixing
records.entry_name: Generic ergodicity and non-smoothness of E₀
records.doc: Eventual equality on the actual Cantor product has a BP invariant-set zero-one law. Every invariant map with BP open preimages into a second countable T0 target has a comeagre constant fiber. Consequently no such BP map, and no Borel map with explicit Borel sigma-algebras, reduces eventual equality to equality.

records.name: Furstenberg.weakMixing_iff_product_transitive
records.entry_name: Furstenberg weak mixing and finite diagonal powers
records.doc: For a continuous self-map of a nonempty topological space, square transitivity implies transitivity of every finite diagonal power, including power zero. A genuine open-pair refinement and finite induction give a common natural forward hitting time for any finite family of nonempty open pairs. The literal two-pair condition is proved equivalent to actual square transitivity.

records.name: LorentzSubmission.common_origin_counterexample
records.entry_name: Self-similar counterexamples to three conjectures of Lorentz
records.doc: Three continuous counterexamples in uniform polynomial approximation: a nonodd function whose best approximants all vanish at zero, a nonodd function with plateaus at degrees (2k+1,2k+2), and a noneven function with plateaus at degrees (2k,2k+1). Exact algebraic certificates, analytic contact persistence, and cubic self-similarity prove all three results. This repository contains the substantive formalization and formalizes the owner-supplied mathematical manuscripts.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.CollapsedGenealogy.all_blocks_iff_collapsed_joint_eq
records.entry_name: Linked-site block laws of all lengths identify the collapsed mutation-scaled genealogy
records.doc: This entry formalizes an identifiability theorem for three sampled sequences whose sites all share one random three-tip genealogy (complete linkage). A genealogy is a pair of branch lengths (u, v), where u is the height of the cherry and v is the length of the upper internal branch, together with a label in Fin 3 recording which pair of tips forms the cherry. Its law is an arbitrary finite measure that is almost everywhere supported on nonnegative branch lengths. Given the genealogy, sites evolve independently under the K-state equal-rates mutation model with a uniform root distribution and mutation scale k. For K ≥ 2 and k, l ≥ 0, two such measures, with scales k and l, produce the same law of block patterns for every number L of linked sites if and only if their collapsed objects agree. The collapsed object is the push-forward of the measure under (u, v, q) ↦ (k u, k v, q), with the cherry label replaced by a fixed value whenever k v = 0. A second statement shows that, for a genealogy with zero upper branch (a star tree), the block-pattern law does not depend on which cherry label is attached.

records.name: ErdosPaperII.theorem_1_2
records.entry_name: Complete-split extremizers for the fractional triangle-cover deficit on chordal graphs
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main result of the author's preprint "Complete-Split Extremizers for a Fractional Triangle-Cover Functional on Chordal Graphs" (Erdős #81 series, Paper II). For a finite simple graph G let τ₃*(G) be its fractional triangle cover number (the least total weight of a nonnegative weighting of vertex pairs giving every triangle weight at least one on its edges) and Φ_τ(G) = |E(G)| − 2τ₃*(G). For every n ≥ 1, every chordal graph on n vertices satisfies Φ_τ(G) ≤ ⌊(2n + 1)²/24⌋, and equality is attained by a complete-split graph K_p ∨ K̄_q with p + q = n (Theorem 1.2). Chordality and fractional triangle covers use the definitions of two registered entries.

records.name: RefinedAbsorption.Faithful2024.theorem_1_7
records.entry_name: Formalizing Delcourt–Postle’s refined absorption in Lean
records.doc: One assembled Lean formalization of principal refined absorption results and their consequences. The selected results include refined omni-absorbers and refiners, labelled reserve matchings, dense compatible decompositions, an additive compatible-absorber interface retaining independence of the entire old ambient vertex set, and existence of simple designs for every fixed q > r ≥ 2 and index λ ≥ 1 at all sufficiently large admissible orders. The literal global embedding conclusion of the survey is refuted separately from a proved piecewise replacement. The research-note endpoints give completion avoiding an arbitrary forbidden partial Steiner system, sparse prescribed and finite embedded exact intersections, an initial polynomial intersection interval, and polynomial excess in partial parallel classes and Nash–Williams schedule rounds. Both external inputs are supplied by pinned proved theorems. The single comparison selects eighteen declarations from the existing aggregate proof root.

records.name: ErdosPaperIII.theorem_1_1
records.entry_name: Linear-error clique partitions of split graphs
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main results of the author's preprint "Linear-Error Clique Partitions of Split Graphs via Structured Triangle Packing" (Erdős #81 series, Paper III): there is an absolute constant C such that every finite split graph G on n vertices satisfies |E(G)| − 2ν₃(G) ≤ n²/6 + C·n, where ν₃(G) is the maximum number of pairwise edge-disjoint triangles (Theorem 1.1); consequently G has a clique partition (a family of cliques covering every edge exactly once) with at most n²/6 + C·n cliques (Corollary 1.2). The quadratic coefficient 1/6 is the sharp one for split graphs. The constant C is existential and not explicit. Two ingredients of the proof, the asymptotic gap between fractional and integral triangle packings and exact triangle decompositions of dense triangle-divisible graphs, are taken from two registered formalizations (see related_formalizations).

records.name: CorradiHajnalTheorem.corradi_hajnal
records.entry_name: The Corrádi–Hajnal theorem on vertex-disjoint cycles
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Corrádi–Hajnal theorem (1963): every finite simple graph on at least 3k vertices with minimum degree at least 2k contains k vertex-disjoint cycles. Cycles are closed walks that are cycles in Mathlib's sense; the theorem is also stated with the definition of disjoint cycles of the registered Erdős–Pósa entry (k pairwise disjoint vertex sets, each inducing a subgraph that is not acyclic). Both hypotheses are shown to be needed: for k ≥ 2 the complete graph on 3k − 1 vertices has minimum degree 3k − 2 ≥ 2k and no k disjoint cycles, and for m ≥ 2k the complete bipartite graph K_{2k−1, m} has at least 3k vertices and minimum degree 2k − 1 and no k disjoint cycles. Mathlib has cycles and minimum degree but not this theorem.

records.name: MoserTardosTheorem.expected_count_le
records.entry_name: The Moser–Tardos theorem (algorithmic Lovász Local Lemma)
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Moser–Tardos theorem in the variable setting: finitely many independent random variables with finite ranges, n events each determined by a finite set of variables, neighbours sharing a variable. If P(A_j) ≤ x_j ∏_{k ∈ Γ(j)} (1 − x_k) with 0 ≤ x_j < 1, the resampling algorithm (always resampling the first violated event), run on a random resampling table, resamples A_j at most x_j / (1 − x_j) times in expectation among its first t steps, for every t; the expected total number of resamplings is at most ∑_j x_j / (1 − x_j); the probability that it has not stopped after t steps is at most (∑_j x_j / (1 − x_j)) / t; and some assignment avoids all events (the Lovász Local Lemma in the variable setting). The proof formalizes witness trees built from the log, the τ-check coupling with the resampling table, and the Galton–Watson bound.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.ComputeTwoLocus.q_correct
records.entry_name: A kernel-checked implementation of the biallelic two-locus sampling recursion, and a table checker
records.doc: This entry states correctness results, in exact rational arithmetic, for an executable implementation of the two-locus sampling recursion of the coalescent with recombination under parent-independent mutation, with two alleles at each locus. For valid parameters and configurations with the stated array sizes, the computation succeeds and its value equals the solution of the recursion at the decoded configuration. A table checker is shown to be sound and complete: a table that passes the check consists of true values of the recursion, and the table of true values over the closure of configurations of a given size passes. The existence of a solution to the recursion, for any finite numbers of alleles, positive mutation rates, and nonnegative recombination rate, is also stated, together with an explicit characterization of the Boolean parameter-validity test.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.ConcreteBettingTest.concrete_uniform_pan_size
records.entry_name: A prespecified betting test of panmixia against a two-deme history: size and power
records.doc: This entry formalizes a prespecified fixed-sample test, based on independent blocks of three linked sites observed at three sampled tips with four allelic states, of a panmictic null model against a two-deme alternative. Under the null, the three-tip genealogy follows the coalescent with a time-varying pair-coalescence rate r, and sites mutate under the four-state equal-rates model with scale k. For every nonnegative locally integrable rate r whose integrated clock diverges and every k > 0, the rejection probability with at least 72,000,000,000 independent blocks is at most 1/20. For one specific two-island alternative, with all three tips sampled in the same deme, the rejection probability is at least 4/5 with exactly 72,000,000,000 blocks and at least 19/20 with exactly 250,000,000,000 blocks. The test, its features, its betting factors, its localization tolerance, and its threshold are fixed numerical choices given in the Challenge.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.DenominatorLaw.T_mulVec_Phi_eq_phiRecursionSource
records.entry_name: An upper bound on the denominators of solutions of the two-locus sampling recursion
records.doc: This entry formalizes degree and divisibility facts about the denominators of solutions to the two-locus sampling recursion with two alleles at each locus. Centred moments of a solution, grouped in blocks by the numbers i and j of lineages at the two loci, satisfy a tridiagonal linear system with matrix T(i, j) whose right-hand side involves only smaller blocks. An explicit product D of linear factors in the mutation rates and of block determinants E(p, s) = det T(p, s) clears the denominator of the solution: D times the solution lies in any subring that contains the parameters. Conditionally on D being the reduced denominator of the top centred moment, every denominator of the solution is divisible by E. The determinant E(i, j) has degree min(i, j) in the recombination rate when a nonvanishing condition holds, and is positive when i, j ≥ 2 and the rates are nonnegative. Two statements show that the diagonal determinants E(m, m), with one mutation rate set to zero, have irreducible factors of unbounded degree as m varies, both as polynomials in the mutation rate over rational functions of the recombination rate and as polynomials in the recombination rate over rational functions of the mutation rate.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.EwensUrn.sum_esf
records.entry_name: The Ewens sampling formula and its generative urn
records.doc: This entry formalizes the Ewens sampling formula for partitions of n and its relation to a generative urn. Over any field of characteristic zero, the weights sum to 1 whenever the rising factorial in θ is nonzero, and they have an explicit product form in the part counts. For θ > 0 the urn law on partitions of n equals the Ewens weights. The conditional law given the number of parts is expressed through Stirling numbers of the first kind, and the weights are consistent under deletion of one sampled individual.

records.name: QuadraticFloor.root_count
records.entry_name: QuadraticFloor: quadratic floor sums and the trace of a quartic Bernoulli number
records.doc: For an odd prime p and integers A, B, C, the alternating floor sum S_{A,B,C}(p) is the sum over 0 <= n < p of (-1)^floor((A n^2 + B n + C)/p). The development proves the root-count reduction of S_{A,B,C}(p) to a sum of Legendre symbols over an arithmetic progression when A + B is even, and, for a positive odd A, an odd prime p not dividing A and an admissible pair (B odd, prime to A, 1 <= B^2 - 4AC < 4A), the square-class decomposition: S_{A,B,C}(p) equals (-1)^C minus the average over the Dirichlet characters psi modulo A of conj(psi(B))^2 times the first Bernoulli number, at modulus 8Ap, of the odd character eta_p chi_{-4}^{delta} psi, where eta_p is the Kronecker character of discriminant -8p. Consequently the sum depends only on the square class of B modulo A. At A = 1 and A = 3 this gives the floor sums in terms of Bernoulli numbers of quadratic characters (which are class numbers by Dirichlet's formula, not formalized). At A = 5 the difference S_{5,3,0}(p) - S_{5,1,0}(p) is the real part of the first Bernoulli number of the quartic character Theta_p = eta_p chi_{-4} xi of conductor 40p, with xi(2) = i; this real part is an even integer whose residue modulo 4 is given by an explicit indicator z_1 - z_3. Finally the sums with A = 1 and fixed shifts a, b are classified: for odd a in terms of S_{1,1,0}(p) and an oriented sum of Legendre symbols, for even a by an explicit finite formula that is bounded and eventually constant in p.

records.name: QuadraticFloor.monic_even_bound
records.entry_name: QuadraticFloor: quadratic floor sums and the trace of a quartic Bernoulli number
records.doc: For an odd prime p and integers A, B, C, the alternating floor sum S_{A,B,C}(p) is the sum over 0 <= n < p of (-1)^floor((A n^2 + B n + C)/p). The development proves the root-count reduction of S_{A,B,C}(p) to a sum of Legendre symbols over an arithmetic progression when A + B is even, and, for a positive odd A, an odd prime p not dividing A and an admissible pair (B odd, prime to A, 1 <= B^2 - 4AC < 4A), the square-class decomposition: S_{A,B,C}(p) equals (-1)^C minus the average over the Dirichlet characters psi modulo A of conj(psi(B))^2 times the first Bernoulli number, at modulus 8Ap, of the odd character eta_p chi_{-4}^{delta} psi, where eta_p is the Kronecker character of discriminant -8p. records.name: PalomarTheorem12.main_result
records.entry_name: Three omitted values and non-Blaschke point divisors in half-planes
records.doc: An unconditional Lean formalization of Theorem 1.2 of arXiv:2608.26062v2: a real meromorphic function has three infinite exceptional fibres on the real axis, while every other point divisor fails the Blaschke condition in each half-plane and the function is not of bounded type in either.

records.name: GraphIsoPalomar.gi_singleTape
records.entry_name: Graph isomorphism in quasipolynomial time on a single-tape Turing machine
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Babai's quasipolynomial-time algorithm for graph isomorphism, without the classification of finite simple groups, carried down to Turing machines. There is a single-tape Turing machine (Mathlib's Turing.TM0) that decides whether two simple graphs on n vertices, given in a fixed encoding, are isomorphic within 2^(c (floor(log2 n) + 1)^8) transitions, and another that within the same bound outputs either "not isomorphic" or an isomorphism τ together with generators of a subgroup whose left coset by τ is exactly the set of all isomorphisms. The algorithm (Luks's framework, Schreier–Sims, Weisfeiler–Leman refinement and the Design Lemma, Split-or-Johnson, local certificates and Babai's recursion, with Pyber's analysis in place of the classification), its cost in an executed cost model, and its compilation to multi-stack and then single-tape machines are all proved in Lean.

records.name: LieTrotter.norm_trotter_sub_le_commutator
records.entry_name: lie-trotter-lean
records.doc: A machine-checked proof of the Lie-Trotter product formula in an arbitrary complete normed algebra over the reals with norm-one unit, with a commutator-scaling error bound: for all A, B and n >= 1, the distance from (exp(A/n) exp(B/n))^n to exp(A + B) is at most ‖AB - BA‖ / (2n) · e^(‖A‖ + ‖B‖).

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.ExplicitFormula.q_eq_qExplicit
records.entry_name: An explicit block-recursive formula for solutions of the two-locus sampling recursion
records.doc: This entry formalizes an explicit block-recursive formula for the solution of the two-locus sampling recursion under parent-independent mutation, with two alleles at each locus, positive mutation rates, and nonnegative recombination rate, over any ordered field. The explicit expression equals every solution of the recursion and is itself a solution, so it is the unique solution. Lumping statements show that merging alleles, by pushing configurations forward along maps between allele sets of any sizes, carries solutions to solutions, and that when every allele class is merged into two classes the lumped values are given by the explicit two-allele formula at the merged allele frequencies. A variant of the explicit formula, for any number of alleles at one locus and two at the other, is shown to equal every solution of the recursion.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.GaloisObstruction.natDegree_E
records.entry_name: Block determinants of the two-locus sampling recursion: degree, positivity, squarefreeness, coprimality, and Galois groups
records.doc: This entry formalizes algebraic properties of the block determinants E(i, j) of the two-locus sampling recursion, viewed as polynomials in the recombination rate ρ. E(i, j) is the determinant of an explicit (min(i, j) + 1)-square tridiagonal matrix whose entries depend on i, j, the mutation rates θ_A and θ_B, and ρ. Its degree in ρ is min(i, j) under a stated nondegeneracy condition, and it is positive for i, j ≥ 2 with nonnegative parameters. For nonnegative real mutation rates, every root in ρ of E(5, 5) and of E(7, 7) is real and negative. At explicit rational parameters with negative θ_A, E(5, 5) and E(7, 7) are irreducible over the rationals, have 3 and 5 real roots, have Galois groups of orders 120 and 5040 (the full symmetric groups), and have roots that are not expressible by radicals. E(5, 5) and E(7, 7) are irreducible over the field of rational functions in the mutation rate, and their Galois groups over the field of rational functions in two independent mutation rates are the full symmetric groups; a general specialization lemma used for this is also stated. Squarefreeness, and coprimality for distinct index pairs, of the determinants with i, j ≥ 1 are stated over a field of rational functions in two independent mutation rates and over a field of Laurent series in which both mutation rates are large with a ratio that is not rational.

Its degree in ρ is min(i, j) under a stated nondegeneracy condition, and it is positive for i, j ≥ 2 with nonnegative parameters. For nonnegative real mutation rates, every root in ρ of E(5, 5) and of E(7, 7) is real and negative. At explicit rational parameters with negative θ_A, E(5, 5) and E(7, 7) are irreducible over the rationals, have 3 and 5 real roots, have Galois groups of orders 120 and 5040 (the full symmetric groups), and have roots that are not expressible by radicals. E(5, 5) and E(7, 7) are irreducible over the field of rational functions in the mutation rate, and their Galois groups over the field of rational functions in two independent mutation rates are the full symmetric groups; a general specialization lemma used for this is also stated. Squarefreeness, and coprimality for distinct index pairs, of the determinants with i, j ≥ 1 are stated over a field of rational functions in two independent mutation rates and over a field of Laurent series in which both mutation rates are large with a ratio that is not rational.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.KingmanSegregatingSites.markedKingmanSegregating_mean
records.entry_name: Mean and variance of segregating sites, Watterson's estimator, and pairwise differences under Kingman's coalescent
records.doc: This entry formalizes the mean and variance of three statistics for a sample of size n ≥ 2 under Kingman's coalescent, with time scaled so that each pair of lineages coalesces at rate 1 and with mutations placed on each branch as a Poisson process of rate θ/2 per unit length (infinite sites, so every mutation is a segregating site). The genealogy is Kingman's coalescent on set partitions of the labelled sample, realized as a jump chain with independent exponential holding times, and the mutation counts on its branch segments are conditionally independent Poisson variables given the genealogy. The statistics are the number S of segregating sites, Watterson's estimator S/a₁, and the average number π of pairwise differences. The mean of S is θa₁ and its variance is θa₁ + θ²a₂, where a₁ = Σ_{i=1}^{n−1} 1/i and a₂ = Σ_{i=1}^{n−1} 1/i². Watterson's estimator has mean θ and variance θ/a₁ + θ²a₂/a₁². The mean of π is θ, and its variance is b₁θ + b₂θ² with b₁ = (n + 1)/(3(n − 1)) and b₂ = 2(n² + n + 3)/(9n(n − 1)).

The statistics are the number S of segregating sites, Watterson's estimator S/a₁, and the average number π of pairwise differences. The mean of S is θa₁ and its variance is θa₁ + θ²a₂, where a₁ = Σ_{i=1}^{n−1} 1/i and a₂ = Σ_{i=1}^{n−1} 1/i². Watterson's estimator has mean θ and variance θ/a₁ + θ²a₂/a₁². The mean of π is θ, and its variance is b₁θ + b₂θ² with b₁ = (n + 1)/(3(n − 1)) and b₂ = 2(n² + n + 3)/(9n(n − 1)).

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.KingmanTrees.card_ranked_labelled_history
records.entry_name: Combinatorics and probabilities of Kingman coalescent trees: histories, shapes, topologies, root splits, Colless, and Sackin
records.doc: This entry formalizes combinatorics and probabilities of trees under Kingman's coalescent, through its embedded jump chain, in which each pair of the k current lineages is the next to merge with probability 1/binomial(k, 2). A ranked labelled history on n leaves is a sequence of n − 1 merges starting from n singletons; there are n!(n − 1)!/2^(n−1) of them, and each has probability 2^(n−1)/(n!(n − 1)!). Ranked and unranked tree shapes are defined as classes of histories under relabelling of the leaves; their numbers satisfy André's recurrence for alternating permutations, shifted by one, and the Wedderburn–Etherington recurrence, respectively, with the cases n = 1 and n = 2. The probability of a labelled rooted binary topology T is 2^(n−1)/(n! ∏(|C| − 1)), the product running over the clades C of T with at least two leaves. The probability that the root splits the leaves into a given set A and its complement is 2/((n − 1) binomial(n, |A|)). The probability that a sample S of a population of N leaves has the population root as its most recent common ancestor is (|S| − 1)(N + 1)/((|S| + 1)(N − 1)), which tends to (n − 1)/(n + 1) for a sample of fixed size n as N tends to infinity. The expected Colless and Sackin indices are n H_{⌊n/2⌋} − 2⌊n/2⌋ and 2n(H_n − 1), where H_m is the m-th harmonic number. Finally, the process of roots of the forest histories is identified with the jump chain of Kingman's partition-valued coalescent, for one step and for t steps.

The probability of a labelled rooted binary topology T is 2^(n−1)/(n! ∏(|C| − 1)), the product running over the clades C of T with at least two leaves. The probability that the root splits the leaves into a given set A and its complement is 2/((n − 1) binomial(n, |A|)). The probability that a sample S of a population of N leaves has the population root as its most recent common ancestor is (|S| − 1)(N + 1)/((|S| + 1)(N − 1)), which tends to (n − 1)/(n + 1) for a sample of fixed size n as N tends to infinity. The expected Colless and Sackin indices are n H_{⌊n/2⌋} − 2⌊n/2⌋ and 2n(H_n − 1), where H_m is the m-th harmonic number. Finally, the process of roots of the forest histories is identified with the jump chain of Kingman's partition-valued coalescent, for one step and for t steps.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.LinkedPairPanel.panel_eq_iff
records.entry_name: Linked-pair panels: panel laws are determined by finitely many Laplace values
records.doc: This entry formalizes panels of linked site pairs observed through a reporting channel, with the pair coalescence time T following a probability law on the non-negative reals. All L sites of a panel share the same time T; given T = t, the sites are reported independently, and at each site the two lineages share one latent type with weight e^(−kt) and have independent types otherwise, each type being reported through a channel that maps K latent types to probability distributions on a finite set of labels. For an informative channel (one whose rows are not all equal) and a panel of length L, the panel laws of two time laws agree for all outcomes if and only if their Laplace transforms agree at the points rk for r = 0, …, L. If the channel erases all information, every panel law agrees. If the transforms agree up to L and differ at the next point, then panels of length L agree but some panel of length L + 1 differs. For k > 0, agreement of all panels of all lengths is equivalent to equality of the time laws.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.NeutralFixation.fixation_real_of_nonDegenerate
records.entry_name: Neutral fixation probability in exchangeable (Cannings) models
records.doc: This entry formalizes the neutral fixation probability in exchangeable (Cannings) models with N individuals. For a non-degenerate model, the probability that the allele count started from i copies ever reaches N equals i/N, and the same holds for eventual absorption in the fixed state. The loss probability is 1 − i/N. For a degenerate model started away from the full state the probability of fixation is 0, and an example with N = 2 shows that the fixation probability can differ from the frequency without a reachability hypothesis. For N ≥ 2, non-degeneracy is shown equivalent to positive-probability reachability of the boundary {0, N} by the count chain, and to each of three conditions on the offspring number of a single parent. A general fixation statement is given for chains on {0, ..., N} whose state is mean-preserving in one step and from which the boundary {0, N} is reachable. The Moran model is shown to be non-degenerate with fixation probability i/N.

records.name: ShannonTheorem.shannon
records.entry_name: Shannon's theorem on edge colourings of multigraphs
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Shannon's theorem (1949): every finite loopless multigraph of maximum degree at most Δ has a proper edge colouring with ⌊3Δ/2⌋ colours; and its sharpness: for every Δ the Shannon triangle (three vertices with ⌊Δ/2⌋, ⌊Δ/2⌋ and ⌈Δ/2⌉ parallel edges between the three pairs) has maximum degree at most Δ and no proper edge colouring with fewer than ⌊3Δ/2⌋ colours. Multigraphs are edge families ends : ι → V × V (parallel edges allowed), a lighter representation than Mathlib's multigraph structure Graph α β (Mathlib.Combinatorics.Graph.Basic: vertex and edge sets with an incidence relation IsLink), which at the pinned revision has no degrees or edge colourings; no bridge to Graph α β is proved. Neither result is in Mathlib.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.NoEwensFormula.boundedDen_eval
records.entry_name: No formula with denominators of bounded degree, in the total mutation parameter or in rho, for the two-locus sampling recursion
records.doc: This entry formalizes results on the degree of denominators of any closed-form expression for the solution of the two-locus sampling recursion of the coalescent with recombination, with two alleles at each locus and parent-independent mutation. The mutation rates, the recombination rate rho, and the allele frequencies are independent indeterminates, and the recursion is solved over a field of rational functions in them. An expression is built from rational constants, arbitrary coefficients from the coefficient field, the rates, sums, products, and quotients; it is admissible at degree D when every divisor evaluates to a nonzero polynomial of degree at most D in a designated variable (rho, or the total mutation rate theta_A + theta_B). A closure lemma shows that admissible expressions in inputs with bounded denominators have bounded denominators. For the sample of two lineages that carry the same haplotype at both loci, no admissible expression of degree one in rho, and none of degree two in the total mutation rate, equals the value of the solution; variants bound the total degree of the divisors in the three rates instead. For the samples of m lineages typed at locus A only and m typed at locus B only, all of allele 0, for every bound D there is an m ≥ 2 at which no admissible expression of degree D, in the total mutation rate or in rho, equals the value of the solution. Existence and uniqueness of the solutions are also stated in these settings.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.PartitionPair.esf_pair_decomposition
records.entry_name: A partition-pair decomposition of the two-locus sampling probability with Ewens marginals
records.doc: This entry formalizes a decomposition of the two-locus sampling probability, under finite-allele parent-independent mutation, in terms of pairs of set partitions of the sample, with Ewens marginals at each locus. A partition-carrying ancestral process with coalescence, mutation, and recombination records, at each locus, which sample members lose their ancestry to the same mutation; the kernel is the probability that it ends with a given pair of partitions. The solution of the two-locus sampling recursion at a fully typed sample is the sum over pairs of partitions of the kernel times the probability that each block receives a single allele consistent with the sample. Summing the kernel over the partition at one locus gives the Ewens partition probability at the other; as the recombination rate tends to infinity the kernel tends to the product of the two Ewens partition probabilities; and with recombination rate 0 the common refinement of the two partitions has the Ewens law with parameter θA + θB. The sampling probability equals the product of its one-locus marginals for all parameter values exactly when at most one lineage is typed at one of the loci (with at least two alleles per locus). A closed form for configurations with two lineages typed at each locus is also stated, together with existence of a solution of the recursion.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.SamplingRecursion.exists_isSolution
records.entry_name: The two-locus sampling recursion of the coalescent with recombination: existence, uniqueness, and probabilistic interpretation
records.doc: This entry formalizes the two-locus sampling recursion of the coalescent with recombination, with finitely many alleles at each locus and parent-independent mutation. For positive mutation rates and nonnegative recombination rate, a solution exists and is unique, over any linearly ordered field. For real parameters, the solution at a sample typed at both loci equals the probability that the typed ancestral recombination graph, in which a mutation removes the ancestry of a lineage at that locus and assigns a type to the sample members it carries, ends with exactly the types of the sample. The solution sums to 1 over all typings of a sample of given size, tends to the product of the one-locus sampling probabilities as the recombination rate tends to infinity, and at recombination rate 0 gives a solution of a one-locus recursion on pairs of alleles. With mutation rates 0, the expected total branch length of the genealogy at locus A of a sample of size n is 2 times the sum of 1/(i + 1) for i < n − 1. The transition matrix of the typed ancestral chain is shown to be nonnegative with unit row sums.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.SevenSiteSeparator.seven_site_separation
records.entry_name: Seven linked sites separate a two-island history from every panmictic history
records.doc: This entry formalizes a statement about blocks of seven completely linked sites with K ≥ 2 equally weighted roots, observed in three sampled sequences under an equal-rates K-state mutation model. A specific two-island history for three lineages (all three lineages start in the same island, the coalescence rate within an island is 1, and the migration rate is 1/100) produces, at mutation scale 1, a law of the seven-site block that differs from the block law of every panmictic history at every mutation scale k > 0. The panmictic histories are those given by a nonnegative locally integrable pairwise coalescence rate whose integrated clock diverges, so the population size may vary arbitrarily in time.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.SmcPrimeBound.eventKernel_isMarkovKernel
records.entry_name: Total variation bound between an unpruned ancestral recombination process and SMC' on pairwise coalescence times
records.doc: This entry formalizes a total variation bound between the pairwise coalescence-time process of an unpruned ancestral recombination graph and the SMC' approximation, for N ≥ 1 samples, a unit-length genome, and scaled recombination rate R ≥ 0. The observed object is the collection of pairwise coalescence times of all sample pairs at every rational position in [0, 1). The total variation distance is at most an explicit double bound, which is at most min(1, R² times a quadratic coefficient in N − 1). The distance is 0 for one sample and for zero recombination. Supporting statements show that the event kernels of both processes are Markov, the two laws are probability measures, the number of live lineages of the backward process reaches at most one almost surely, the observed coalescence times are almost surely finite, and the expected number of active events, the expected total time, and the expected largest observed coalescence time are bounded by an explicit absorption budget.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.TajimaD.markedKingmanLaw_probability
records.entry_name: Tajima's D under Kingman's coalescent: moments of the numerator, the variance estimate, and the expected spectrum
records.doc: This entry formalizes Tajima's D under Kingman's coalescent with infinitely many sites and mutation parameter θ ≥ 0, for sample size n ≥ 2. The joint law of the genealogy and the mutation counts on its branches is a probability measure. The mean of the numerator is 0 and its variance equals c₁ θ + c₂ θ², where c₁ and c₂ are Tajima's coefficients. The covariance of the pairwise-difference statistic with the number of segregating sites and the mean of their product are stated. The variance estimate based on the number of segregating sites is unbiased for that variance. The expected value of the site frequency spectrum at frequency i is θ/i for 1 ≤ i < n, and these values sum to the mean number of segregating sites; the closed-form coefficient of the expected spectrum equals θ/i and equals that mean. D is defined to be 0 when the variance estimate is nonpositive, and as a result it is 0 when there are no segregating sites and for n = 2 and n = 3; D is a measurable function of the sample.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.WeakRegularSeparation.nonnegative_internal_branch_separation_iff
records.entry_name: When one finite block of linked sites separates a three-sample genealogy from every panmictic history
records.doc: This entry formalizes conditions under which a single finite block of linked sites separates a three-sample genealogy from every panmictic history. A law of the two coalescence-interval lengths and the tree shape of three sampled sequences is uniformly separated at mutation scale k > 0 when some block of L completely linked sites, observed under the equal-rates mutation model, has a law at ℓ1 distance at least a fixed ε > 0 from the block law of every panmictic history (any nonnegative, locally integrable, time-varying coalescence rate with a diverging integrated clock), at every mutation scale and for every alphabet size K ≥ 2. For laws with nonnegative interval lengths, a positive first coalescence time, and a regular first-survival profile matching the first coalescence time, uniform separation holds if and only if the law differs from the panmictic law with the profile's rate, in which the tree shape is uniform and independent of the times; a version for laws of the interval lengths alone, with a uniform independent shape, is also given. For three-sample symmetric island histories with time-varying coalescence and migration rates under the stated integrability hypotheses, uniform separation holds if and only if the history is not the one with all three lineages starting in the same island, no migration, and a diverging integrated coalescence clock. For finite-phase histories, separation is equivalent to failure of a density identity characterizing the panmictic form.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.SelectionTheorems.fisher_fundamental_theorem
records.entry_name: Classical identities and a limit theorem of selection theory
records.doc: This entry collects classical identities and a limit theorem from selection theory. The identities are stated for finite populations; Geiringer's limit theorem is stated for the deterministic infinite-population recombination model on finitely many loci with a common finite allele set. Fisher's fundamental theorem is stated, in Ewens' interpretation, as the equality of the partial change in mean fitness (the change in allele frequencies under selection, weighted by least-squares average effects) with the additive genetic variance divided by mean fitness, for arbitrary genotype frequencies and any number of loci, together with nonnegativity of that change. A grouped covariance decomposition and a multilevel Price equation are stated as identities for arbitrary weights. Hamilton's rule is derived from the least-squares regression of fitness on own and social genotypes, and the existence of the Lande–Arnold gradient, equal to the inverse phenotypic covariance matrix applied to the vector of selection differentials, is stated under a nonsingular phenotypic covariance. Geiringer's theorem is stated as convergence of repeated recombination to the product of the single-locus marginals, under the condition that every pair of loci is separated with positive probability.

records.name: ThickSensitive.separated_open_targets
records.entry_name: Weak mixing and thick common multi-sensitivity
records.doc: A continuous surjective weakly mixing map on a nontrivial metric space admits one positive separation constant such that every finite family of nonempty open sets has arbitrarily long, arbitrarily late blocks of common positive separation times. Witness pairs may depend on the set and time. Finite-family common hitting thickness and separated open targets are proved.

records.name: CKM.NativeTightCodeConsumer.code_bound
records.entry_name: On the local geometry of the tight 39-point code in 𝕆P²
records.doc:
Cohn, Kumar and Minton constructed a universally optimal code of thirty-nine points in the octonionic projective plane 𝕆P², whose existence was conjectured by Hoggar. Its points form thirteen mutually unbiased Jordan frames, and a four-parameter phase family deforms the code through such configurations. This Lean development describes their local geometry under the automorphism group F₄. At every nonresonant phase, every nearby real solution of the defining equations belongs to one of four smooth families of labelled configurations. In a local slice for F₄, their union has normal form R⁴ × ⋃ᵢ₌₁⁴ R⁶ᵢ, with the R⁶ᵢ in direct sum. The distance to the localized family union is bounded by a phase-dependent constant times the square root of the residual, and the exponent 1/2 is sharp in the ambient configuration space. On an explicit open dense subset of the nonresonant phases, the complexified families are exactly the top-dimensional components of the complex solution germ, each generically reduced. Every neighbourhood of the original code in the space of unlabelled tight 39-point codes modulo F₄ contains points of local dimension 10.

The results are local, the resonant germ at the original code is not classified, and lower-dimensional complex components are not excluded. For exact frames and strongly convex C² overlap potentials, we prove a two-sided comparison of the energy gap with squared overlap errors and, near each nonresonant orbit, a quartic lower bound in distance to the localized family union. Except for attributed third-party material, all text and code are AI-generated under Robert R. MacGregor’s direction. Robert is an amateur who welcomes collaboration (macgregor@gmail.com).

Its points form thirteen mutually unbiased Jordan frames, and a four-parameter phase family deforms the code through such configurations. records.name: LeanLab.AlmostPrimes.U1504DudekAll.dudek_all_ap12
records.entry_name: On the sum of a prime and a square-free number
records.doc: Conditional on one explicit hypothesis, AP12Lower 0.21, taken as a hypothesis of the theorem and never as an axiom: for every integer x >= 10^9, each reduced residue class mod 12 holds more than 0.21 x / log x primes p <= x. Under it, a complete Lean 4 proof of Theorem 1 of A. W. Dudek, On the sum of a prime and a square-free number, The Ramanujan Journal 42, 2017: every integer N > 2 is the sum of a prime and a square-free number. AP12Lower 0.21 is implied by Corollary 1.6 of M. A. Bennett, G. Martin, K. O'Bryant and A. Rechnitzer, Explicit bounds for primes in arithmetic progressions, Illinois J. Math. 62, 2018, which gives 1/4 in place of 0.21; the entry proves that implication in Lean, with the corollary itself stated as a hypothesis. The even case, every even N >= 4, is proved with no hypothesis. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. The Lean code was written by an AI agent and is offered for human audit.

records.name: SidonSubmission.sidon_fourier_uniformity
records.entry_name: Extremal Sidon sets: Fourier uniformity and partition regularity
records.doc: A Lean formalization of Ortega and Prendiville's results on Sidon sets in integer intervals. It proves Fourier bounds for near-maximal and largest Sidon sets, equidistribution in progressions and Bohr sets, and monochromatic solutions to partition regular linear equations in at least five variables. It also proves sharp obstruction constructions and records a correction to the paper's dimension-independent approximation claim.

records.name: AuslanderYorke.equicontinuous_of_stable_open_sets
records.entry_name: Auslander–Yorke dichotomy for minimal metric maps
records.doc: For a continuous map of a metric space with every forward natural orbit dense, either the map is sensitive in the open-set pair sense or its natural iterate family is equicontinuous at every point. Stable open sets are propagated using dense orbits and finite early-time continuity. On nonempty spaces nonsensitivity is equivalent to equicontinuity; no compactness or uniform-equicontinuity assertion is required.

records.name: PalomarC3a.c3a_gt_121418
records.entry_name: A finite two-temperature lower bound for the GHR sum-difference constant
records.doc: The Gyarmati-Hennecart-Ruzsa constant C₃ₐ is the supremum of real exponents theta for which every K > 1 admits a positive constant c and arbitrarily large nonempty finite integer sets X with nonempty partners Y satisfying |X+Y| <= K|X| and c|X+Y|^theta <= |X-Y|. This formalization proves the strict bound C₃ₐ > 60709/50000 = 1.21418. A finite type at depth 10^13, separate difference and sum tilts, cyclic compression, and a proved finite-set principle supply the bound. The result concerns extremal sumset and difference-set growth in additive combinatorics. The paper's general limiting theorem is outside the formalized claim.

records.name: InfHarmonic.main_estimate
records.entry_name: Uniform interior C^{1,α} estimates for infinity-harmonic functions in dimensions d ≥ 3
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main results of the preprint "Uniform Interior C^{1,α} Estimates for Infinity-Harmonic Functions" (OpenAI, 2026). For every dimension d ≥ 3 there are α ∈ (0, 1/3] and C < ∞ such that every bounded viscosity solution u of the infinity-Laplace equation Δ_∞u = Σ u_i u_j u_ij = 0 on the unit ball of ℝ^d is differentiable on the half ball, with sup |∇u| + [∇u]_{C^{0,α}} ≤ C · osc u (Theorem 1.1). Consequently every infinity-harmonic function on a connected open subset of ℝ^d, d ≥ 3, is C¹ (Corollary 1.2). The proof rests on a Liouville theorem for the degenerate limiting equation D²v[(∇ₓv, 1)] = 0 on space-time, for entire solutions admitting uniform affine fits at all scales (Theorem 3.1), which is also formalized. All three results are proved from Mathlib with no sorry and no axioms beyond propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, including the Crandall–Ishii–Lions theorem of sums and Alexandrov's theorem used along the way.

records.name: GeoSeqV4.halton_not_quasiUniform
records.entry_name: Low-discrepancy quasi-uniform digital sequences in every dimension (Halton-type failure and residue sequences)
records.doc:
Two results of the manuscript "Low-discrepancy quasi-uniform digital sequences in every dimension" (version 1): Corollary cor:halton of Theorem thm:nonqu, and Theorem thm:residue with Corollaries cor:korobov and cor:residueQU for one explicit sequence. Quasi-uniform means here: there is a real B such that h(P_[N]) <= B delta(P_[N]) for every N >= 2, where P_[N] is the set of the first N points, h is the Euclidean covering radius of [0,1]^s (a supremum over the cube of the minimum distance to the points) and delta is the minimum Euclidean distance over pairs of distinct indices. (1) For every prime p, every s >= 2 and all pairwise coprime polynomials b_0, ..., b_(s-1) over Z/pZ of degree >= 1, the Halton-type sequence in these bases (Goda-Hofer-Suzuki, Def. 2: coordinate c of the point with index n = sum_k n_k p^k reads the b_c-adic digits (V div b_c^Q) mod b_c of V = sum_k n_k z^k, each written as its deg(b_c) coefficients, the coefficient of z^(deg(b_c)-1) first) is not quasi-uniform, and for every eps > 0 there are m and two distinct indices v, w < p^m whose points have Euclidean distance less than eps (p^m)^(-1/s). For every prime p and every s such bases exist. (2) Let s >= 2, let p > 2^s be prime and rho = floor(p^(1/s)). Consider the residue sequence with the Faure places a_c = c, scale theta = 1 and the Korobov check vector v = (rho, rho^2, ..., rho^(s-1), -1): the digital sequence over Z/pZ with generator matrices C_c[n][i] = v_c^(-1) [t^n] (c + t)^i w_c(c + t)^(-(n+1)), w_c(z) = prod_(c' != c) (z - c'), and coordinates y_c = sum_n y_(c,n) p^(-n-1) with digits in {0, ..., p-1}. It is a (0,s)-sequence in base p; for every K >= 1, any two distinct indices u, u' < N = p^(sK-1) give points at toroidal Euclidean distance (sum_c (d_c - round(d_c))^2)^(1/2), d = difference of the points, at least (rho - 1) p^(-1/s) N^(-1/s); and it is quasi-uniform. Moreover rho >= 2 and rho^s < p, every v_c is nonzero, the places are distinct, and the power series w_c(c + t) over Z/pZ times its inverse is 1. (The entry states no discrepancy bound; that (0,s)-sequences have low discrepancy is classical and is not part of this entry.)
Comparator configuration: comparatorHeadlineSeqV4.json (4 compared theorems, all proved, no sorry): GeoSeqV4.halton_not_quasiUniform, GeoSeqV4.halton_bases_exist, GeoSeqV4.residue_quasiUniform, GeoSeqV4.residue_data. The Challenge (HeadlineSeqV4/Challenge.lean, 195 lines) imports only Mathlib and defines everything it uses from scratch (digital sequences from infinite generator matrices over ZMod p, the (0,s)-sequence property, Euclidean and toroidal distances, covering radius, minimum distance, quasi-uniformity, the Halton-type points, the residue generator matrices). The Solution (HeadlineSeqV4/Solution.lean) imports a verbatim copy of these definitions (HeadlineSeqV4/Defs.lean, generated by scripts/gen_headline_seq_v4_defs.py) and the full formalization GeoSeq of the same Lake project, proves bridge lemmas (each definition equals the corresponding GeoSeq definition) and obtains the theorems from compared theorems of GeoSeq (configurations comparatorGeoSeqV9.json, comparatorGeoSeqV93.json).

Quasi-uniform means here: there is a real B such that h(P_[N]) <= B delta(P_[N]) for every N >= 2, where P_[N] is the set of the first N points, h is the Euclidean covering radius of [0,1]^s (a supremum over the cube of the minimum distance to the points) and delta is the minimum Euclidean distance over pairs of distinct indices. (1) For every prime p, every s >= 2 and all pairwise coprime polynomials b_0, ..., b_(s-1) over Z/pZ of degree >= 1, the Halton-type sequence in these bases (Goda-Hofer-Suzuki, Def. 2: coordinate c of the point with index n = sum_k n_k p^k reads the b_c-adic digits (V div b_c^Q) mod b_c of V = sum_k n_k z^k, each written as its deg(b_c) coefficients, the coefficient of z^(deg(b_c)-1) first) is not quasi-uniform, and for every eps > 0 there are m and two distinct indices v, w < p^m whose points have Euclidean distance less than eps (p^m)^(-1/s). For every prime p and every s such bases exist. (2) Let s >= 2, let p > 2^s be prime and rho = floor(p^(1/s)). Consider the residue sequence with the Faure places a_c = c, scale theta = 1 and the Korobov check vector v = (rho, rho^2, ..., rho^(s-1), -1): the digital sequence over Z/pZ with generator matrices C_c[n][i] = v_c^(-1) [t^n] (c + t)^i w_c(c + t)^(-(n+1)), w_c(z) = prod_(c' != c) (z - c'), and coordinates y_c = sum_n y_(c,n) p^(-n-1) with digits in {0, ..., p-1}. It is a (0,s)-sequence in base p; for every K >= 1, any two distinct indices u, u' < N = p^(sK-1) give points at toroidal Euclidean distance (sum_c (d_c - round(d_c))^2)^(1/2), d = difference of the points, at least (rho - 1) p^(-1/s) N^(-1/s); and it is quasi-uniform. Moreover rho >= 2 and rho^s < p, every v_c is nonzero, the places are distinct, and the power series w_c(c + t) over Z/pZ times its inverse is 1. (The entry states no discrepancy bound; that (0,s)-sequences have low discrepancy is classical and is not part of this entry.)
Comparator configuration: comparatorHeadlineSeqV4.json (4 compared theorems, all proved, no sorry): GeoSeqV4.halton_not_quasiUniform, GeoSeqV4.halton_bases_exist, GeoSeqV4.residue_quasiUniform, GeoSeqV4.residue_data. The Challenge (HeadlineSeqV4/Challenge.lean, 195 lines) imports only Mathlib and defines everything it uses from scratch (digital sequences from infinite generator matrices over ZMod p, the (0,s)-sequence property, Euclidean and toroidal distances, covering radius, minimum distance, quasi-uniformity, the Halton-type points, the residue generator matrices). The Solution (HeadlineSeqV4/Solution.lean) imports a verbatim copy of these definitions (HeadlineSeqV4/Defs.lean, generated by scripts/gen_headline_seq_v4_defs.py) and the full formalization GeoSeq of the same Lake project, proves bridge lemmas (each definition equals the corresponding GeoSeq definition) and obtains the theorems from compared theorems of GeoSeq (configurations comparatorGeoSeqV9.json, comparatorGeoSeqV93.json).

records.name: IPTransitive.weak_mixing_infinite_hits
records.entry_name: Generic IP-transitive points in weakly mixing systems
records.doc: For a continuous map of a second-countable Baire Hausdorff space with topologically transitive square, a residual set of points has IP entering times into every nonempty open set. A nonempty space has a nonempty dense G-delta family of such points; square hitting times are infinite.
